article.articleHeadline: Siberia, muore una tecnica dell'istituto antipeste e 200 persone finiscono in osservazione: Mosca parla di polmonite
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Siberia, a technique from the anti-plague institute dies and 200 people are placed under observation: Moscow talks of pneumonia.
article.articleSummary: Suspected pneumonic plague in the Irkutsk region, Russia. A broken vial on Sept 25 at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute—historic center for dangerous infections—preceded the death of Darya Shipilova, who died Oct 2 after ICU admission Sept 29. About 200 people exposed were placed under medical observation; 189 were hospitalized across two regional hospitals and the institute. Tass said tests conducted for her work found no pathogens linked to the institute; Rospotrebnadzor denied a plague diagnosis. Two hypotheses, a Thailand trip and a lab incident, were examined with none confirmed. Officials say the region’s health status is stable, but four Irkutsk-area hospitals have been quarantined for three weeks. Pneumonic plague is airborne and treatable with antibiotics if treated early. U.S. officials monitor the situation; a lab-safety investigation has been opened.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: COVID-19 remains above the high alert threshold / Children account for 40 percent of influenza-positive cases in the country.
article.articleSummary: Iran's Week 28 surveillance (ending Oct 1, 2026) shows COVID-19 activity remains above the high‑alert threshold, while influenza activity is rising modestly. Among outpatients with influenza‑like illness (ILI) and inpatients with severe acute respiratory infection (SARI), 9.3% and 9.7% respectively had respiratory infections; overall, 8.1% of outpatients and 10.5% of inpatients were positive for respiratory illness. From 203 respiratory samples tested for ILI/SARI, influenza positivity was 2.9% (versus 0.9% the previous year); COVID‑19 positives declined to 13.7% after peaking at 17.4% in the prior week. Laboratory surveillance (5,845 samples) detected 155 influenza positives (2.7%), with 77.5% type B; children accounted for 39.3% of positives (under 2 years 7.7%; 2–5 years 14.2%; 6–15 years 17.4%). Bushehr (18.7%) and Fars (11.6%) exceed high‑alert thresholds; Khuzestan (7.3%) and Kerman (6%) exceed low thresholds. Globally, COVID‑19 is low, RSV stable, while East Asia reports rising influenza and Korea sees more hospitalizations. WHO tracks variants PQ.16.1.1, NB.1.1.1, XFG, BA.3.2; XFG ~41% of sequences.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Rise of falciparum malaria: if left untreated, kidneys and brain may fail. How to stay vigilant?
article.articleSummary: Falciparum malaria, the most dangerous malaria parasite (Plasmodium falciparum), has been detected in Mumbai and across several locations in India during the monsoon season, with climate-driven mosquito proliferation implicated by WHO researchers. If untreated, this malaria can cause cerebral malaria, coma, or death. The disease is transmitted by female Anopheles mosquitoes; four human Plasmodium species exist—vivax, falciparum, ovale, and malariae—with P. falciparum causing malignant malaria. Symptoms include sudden high fever with chills, persistent elevated temperature, severe headache, muscle cramps, diarrhea, nausea, and abdominal bloating; the parasite destroys red blood cells, causing anemia. In the brain, disrupted blood flow can lead to unconsciousness or coma. Prevention focuses on eliminating standing water, using mosquito nets in high-risk areas, and keeping surroundings clean; fever persisting three days warrants a blood test.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: France reaffirms its support for efforts to combat Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: France reaffirms its support for Ebola response in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot, in a post on X, said Paris will deepen backing for researchers, health workers, and humanitarian staff fighting the outbreak. He visited Bunia in eastern DRC, described as the outbreak’s epicenter, where about 8,000 confirmed Ebola cases and 4,000 deaths have been reported, roughly a quarter of them children. Bunia has hosted the outbreak response leadership since May. Containment so far has prevented spread to major African urban centers or to French overseas territories and Europe. France has acted from day one to support frontline professionals. Barrot stressed that viruses do not respect borders and that eradicating Ebola requires addressing root causes, praising the globally recognized expertise of French responders.

triage.headline_ja: フランス、コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ対策支援を再確認
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で約8,000例・4,000人死亡という大規模なエボラ流行が継続しており、国際支援（フランス）も動員されているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当しフルRRAが必要と判断。
triage.notes: 記事はフランスの支援表明に関するものだが、背景にあるDRCのエボラ流行自体が大規模・深刻であるためPICKUPと判定。フランスは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。

article.articleHeadline: रूस में बनाया जा रहा था कोरोना जैसा वायरस? साइबेरिया की लैब में विस्फोट से हड़कंप
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Was a coronavirus-like virus being developed in Russia? Panic after explosion at a Siberian lab.
article.articleSummary: In Russia’s Irkutsk region, a suspected pneumonic plague case emerged after a test tube containing Yersinia pestis broke on Sept 25 at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute in Shelekhov, involving 28-year-old technician Darya Shipilova. She developed severe pneumonia, was admitted Sept 29, placed on a ventilator, and died Oct 1–2. Rospotrebnadzor reported pneumonia of unknown cause and said no pathogen linked to work activity; no confirmed plague or lab accident. About 197 contacts were identified, with roughly 189 under medical surveillance: 114 in one center, 63 in another, and 12 at the anti-plague institute. Five Irkutsk hospitals reportedly quarantined; an aluminum plant in Shelekhov mandated masks from Oct 3. The US CDC and other agencies are monitoring for possible pneumonic plague transmission; no confirmed cases yet. Pneumonic plague spreads via respiratory droplets and is highly dangerous, though early antibiotics can be effective. WHO notes Congo and Madagascar as major sources for plague cases in 2019–2025.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアでコロナウイルスのようなウイルスが開発されていたのか？シベリアの研究所での爆発事故でパニック
triage.triage_reason: ロシア・イルクーツクの抗ペスト研究所でのペスト菌（Yersinia pestis）実験事故により技術者が肺ペストで死亡し、約190名が監視下に置かれている。重大な公衆衛生影響と異常性が認められ、IHR基準2項目以上に該当するためフルRRAへ進める。
triage.notes: 事件はロシア・イルクーツク州シェレホフの抗ペスト研究所内での検体破損事故によるもの。記事中にDRCおよびマダガスカルへの言及があるが、これはWHOによるペスト症例の一般的文脈説明であり、本事件の発生地ではないため verified_locations から除外した。対象国リストにロシアは含まれないため、verified_locationsは空配列とした。

article.articleHeadline: China's vaccine assistance strengthens Pakistan's livestock disease-control efforts
article.articleSummary: China donated 300,000 veterinary vaccine doses to Pakistan to curb lumpy skin disease (LSD) and Brucella melitensis, strengthening a livestock sector that provides 62.45% of agricultural value addition and 14.64% of GDP (FY2025-26). Pakistan’s 2024 Agricultural Census counts 55.86m cattle, 47.74m buffaloes, 44.59m sheep and 95.83m goats. The World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) prioritizes vaccination, early detection, biosecurity and movement controls for LSD, while brucellosis is a zoonosis with economic impact. The aid highlights the need for a sustained system of surveillance, vaccination, cold-chain management, animal identification and vaccination records, and an upgraded electronic Animal Disease Reporting and Surveillance System under One Health. FY2025-26 meat exports totalled 114,046 t worth $530.25m; China imported 2.38m kg beef in 2025, up 177% YoY. The next phase should emphasize tech transfer, diagnostics, labs and local vaccine production, with integrated traceability and export certification, including FMD control, under CPEC Phase II.

triage.headline_ja: 中国のワクチン支援がパキスタンの家畜疾病対策を強化
triage.triage_reason: パキスタンにおける既知の家畜疾病（LSD・ブルセラ症）への中国からのワクチン支援に関する内容であり、ヒトの感染症アウトブレイクや異常事態の報告ではない。対象国リストに該当する発生国も特定できない。
triage.notes: 記事はパキスタンの家畜疾病対策支援に関する内容。中国は支援提供国・輸入国として言及されているのみで、疾病発生国ではない。パキスタンは対象国リストに含まれないため、verified_locationsは空配列。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola cases surge to 8,376 in DR Congo
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has reached 8,376 confirmed cases with 4,042 deaths, per Congolese health authorities (WAM). The ongoing transmission in the DRC poses cross-border risks to neighboring countries as population movement continues. Dr. Jean Kaseya, Director-General of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, warned of heightened risk to neighboring nations while transmission persists. The World Health Organization also cautioned that sustained transmission in the DRC maintains a risk of cross-border spread, reinforcing the need for strengthened surveillance, cross-border coordination, and public health measures in affected and neighboring areas. These figures reflect current outbreak dynamics as of 5 October 2026.

triage.headline_ja: DRCでエボラ症例が8,376人に急増
triage.triage_reason: 致死率が高く大規模な感染者・死者数（8,376症例、4,042死亡）を伴うエボラ流行が継続しており、国境を越えた拡大リスクがWHO・アフリカCDCにより警告されているためIHR基準・WPRO基準複数該当。
triage.notes: 死亡率約48%と高く、WHO・Africa CDCが国境を越えた拡散リスクを警告。近隣国への波及が懸念されるため継続的な監視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Frankreich bekräftigt Unterstützung für den Kampf gegen Ebola in der Demokratischen Republik Kongo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: France reaffirms its support for the fight against Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: France reaffirmed its support for the Ebola response in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), with Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot pledging expanded assistance to researchers, health workers, and relief personnel to end the outbreak. In a late Sunday post on X, following a visit to Bunia in the eastern DRC, Barrot described Bunia as the outbreak’s epicenter and cited roughly 8,000 confirmed infections and 4,000 deaths, about a quarter of them children. Since May of last year Bunia has served as the operational hub for the epidemic-control measures. He noted that containment has prevented spread to major African cities, French overseas territories, and Europe. France says it acted from day one to support scientists and frontline responders, stressing that viruses know no borders and that root-focused measures are needed. Barrot praised French researchers and aid workers combating the outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: フランス、コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ出血熱対策への支援を改めて表明
triage.triage_reason: DRCで確認症例約8000人・死亡約4000人という深刻な被害が続くエボラ流行であり、IHR基準（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常性）を2つ満たすためフルリスク評価に進むべき。
triage.notes: 記事はフランス外相のSNS投稿に基づくもので、具体的な新規症例数や封じ込め状況の詳細な時系列は不明。既存の大規模エボラ流行の継続報道であり、フルRRAでの最新疫学データ確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: هشدار وزارت بهداشت درباره عفونت‌های تنفسی؛ کرونا هنوز بالاتر از آستانه هشدار بالا/ ۴۰ درصد موارد مثبت آنفلوانزا در کودکان
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ministry of Health warns about respiratory infections; COVID-19 remains above the high alert threshold / 40 percent of influenza-positive cases are in children.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 remains above Iran’s high-alert threshold in the latest respiratory-surveillance week ending 11 Mehr. Influenza positives are 15 of 5,845 samples (2.7%), with influenza B comprising the majority. About 39.3% of influenza positives are children, including 7.7% under age 2; 2–5 and 6–15-year-olds account for 14.2% and 17.4%. In clinical surveillance, 9.3% of outpatients with ILI and 9.7% of inpatients with SARI tested positive; weekly ILI among outpatients was 8.1%, SARI 10.5%. SARS-CoV-2 positivity stands at 13.7% of tested samples, after a prior week peak. Bushehr and Fars exceed high-alert influenza thresholds; Khuzestan, Chaharmahal Bakhtiari, and Kerman exceed lower thresholds. Globally, East Asia shows rising influenza with Korea hospitalizations; WHO tracks PQ.16.1.1, NB.1.1.1, XFG, BA.3.2, with XFG dominating sequences.

triage.headline_ja: 保健省、呼吸器感染症について警告;新型コロナは依然として高警戒閾値を上回る/インフルエンザ陽性例の40%は子供
triage.triage_reason: イランにおける季節性の呼吸器感染症サーベイランス報告であり、COVID-19とインフルエンザの流行状況を示すが、対象国（中国等）での独自の異常事態とは言えず、継続監視が妥当。
triage.notes: 主な発生地はイラン（対象国リスト外）。中国・韓国は世界的動向として言及されているのみで、記事の主題ではないため verified_locations には含めない。

article.articleHeadline: प्रयागराज में डेंगू का फैला दायरा, अब तक मरीजों की संख्या बढ़कर हुई 88, SRN अस्पताल में क्या है व्यवस्था? - prayagraj dengue cases rise to 88 government hospitals prepared including srn
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue spread widens in Prayagraj; the number of patients has risen to 88 so far. What arrangements are in place at SRN Hospital?
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever outbreak widens in Prayagraj with 88 cases reported to date in October, after a slower September. In Swaroop Rani Nehru (SRN) Hospital, a 30-bed dengue ward currently has six patients; eight dengue-suspected cases were brought to the Medicine Emergency on Sunday, with four admitted and samples sent to pathology; results are due Monday. Calvin and Bailey Hospital runs a 25-bed dengue ward and had four dengue patients admitted by Sunday; Beli Hospital (TB Saproo) runs a 20-bed dengue ward with four dengue patients admitted by Sunday, after six new admissions on Saturday. Community health centers reserve five beds each for dengue. Authorities note most dengue patients come from urban areas; platelet transfusion is pursued only when the patient is critically ill. Stocks of essential medicines and bed nets are reported, and patient health is improving under the current management.

triage.headline_ja: プラヤグラージでデング熱が拡大、患者数88人に増加 ― SRN病院の対応状況は？
triage.triage_reason: 季節性のデング熱流行で、病院側は病床確保など対応済みであり深刻な公衆衛生上の異常事態とは言えないが、ベクター媒介感染症として拡大の可能性があるため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: インド・ウッタルプラデーシュ州プラヤグラージ（旧アラハバード）での季節性デング熱流行。病院は病床・医薬品を確保し対応中で、重症化例は限定的。結核(TB)は病院名（TB Saproo）に含まれるのみで実際の感染症イベントとは無関係。

article.articleHeadline: Jharkhand: 30 students report vomiting, diarrhoea after educational trip in Khunti
article.articleSummary: In Jharkhand's Khunti district, at least 30 PM Shri High School students from Tilmi fell ill after an educational trip to a gurukul at Dodma and Rani Falls in Torpa block on Oct 3. Symptoms—vomiting, diarrhoea, high fever, and abdominal pain—began Sunday evening, with more cases by Monday morning. Several children were admitted to Karra Community Health Centre; their condition is stable. The district hospital is on alert. Health authorities launched an investigation to determine whether contaminated food prepared during the trip or roadside food near the picnic site caused the illness; the source has not yet been confirmed. Doorto-door checks are underway in Tilmi, Masko, and Barwadag to identify additional cases, while medical teams provide medicines and monitor potential spread.

triage.headline_ja: ジャールカンド州:クンティでの遠足後に学生30人が嘔吐・下痢を報告
triage.triage_reason: 食中毒の疑いで学生30人が発症し入院例もあるが、原因未特定かつ地域的な単発事例であり国際的拡大リスクは低いため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 原因は食中毒の疑いであり感染症との確証はないが、複数名の発症と入院があるため経過観察対象とする。スウェーデンの地名はジオコーディングの誤りと判断し除外。

article.articleHeadline: When a 'Clean' Spinal Tap Deceives: Adenovirus Strikes
article.articleSummary: Four previously healthy toddlers (ages 13–26 months) at Vietnam National Children's Hospital developed fulminant, multiorgan adenovirus infection during June–December 2022. Adenovirus DNA was detected by real-time PCR in both cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and nasopharyngeal samples, indicating systemic infection with CNS involvement, even though CSF cell counts were near normal (1–3 cells/μL) and protein levels low (0.38–0.62 g/L). Neuroimaging in two cases showed bilateral frontoparietal cortical lesions in one patient and nonspecific frontoparietal subarachnoid space widening in the other, consistent with brain injury in immunocompetent children. All four required invasive mechanical ventilation; one required extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and renal replacement therapy. Marked hyperferritinemia was noted, with two clinically diagnosed with macrophage activation syndrome; HLH criteria were not fully evaluated. The report underscores that a normal-appearing spinal tap does not exclude CNS adenovirus disease and suggests immunomodulatory approaches if hyperinflammation contributes to deterioration.

triage.headline_ja: 「クリーン」な脊髄穿刺が欺く時：アデノウイルスが脳と全身を襲う
triage.triage_reason: 2022年6-12月にベトナムの一病院で発生した4例の重症アデノウイルス感染症例報告（学術的ケースシリーズ）であり、新興感染症の発生や公衆衛生上の緊急性を示す情報はない。疾患タグ（豚熱）も記事内容と無関係。
triage.notes: 記事はアデノウイルスによる小児の重症CNS合併症に関する2022年の後ろ向き症例報告であり、公衆衛生上のアウトブレイクではなく医学的知見の共有が目的。Bluedotの疾患タグ（Classical Swine Fever）は誤分類と思われる。

article.articleHeadline: Cảnh giác với các dịch bệnh truyền nhiễm thời điểm giao mùa và cuối năm
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Be vigilant against infectious diseases during seasonal transitions and at the year's end.
article.articleSummary: Vietnam reports over 94,000 dengue cases this year, with 14 deaths, and more than 74,000 hand-foot-mouth disease cases (11 deaths); 5,143 suspected measles; 242 viral encephalitis (1 death); 34 meningococcal meningitis (5 deaths); and 54 rabies deaths. Dengue is rising across provinces during the rainy season. In Ho Chi Minh City, 21–27 September recorded over 1,400 dengue cases; year-to-date totals exceed 35,000. Hand-foot-mouth in the same period reached 1,538 cases, with 36,676 cumulative by week 39. Severe dengue cases include two youths (ages 16 and 21) requiring ECMO and prolonged dialysis; a 20-year-old died in September in HCMC. At the central hospital, dengue presents diversely, including cases after travel and in cancer patients. Hanoi reports dengue in a 49-year-old and a 37-year-old after travel. Authorities urge early medical assessment, avoid NSAIDs before dengue is ruled out, and reinforce mosquito control and personal protection.

triage.headline_ja: 季節の変わり目と年末における感染症への警戒
triage.triage_reason: ベトナムにおける季節性のデング熱・手足口病等の年次サーベイランス報告であり、重症例や死亡例はあるものの、例年の流行パターンの範囲内とみられ、新規性・異常性は低い。複数疾患の動向は継続注視が必要。
triage.notes: 複数疾患（デング熱、手足口病、麻疹疑い、ウイルス性脳炎、髄膜炎菌性髄膜炎、狂犬病）の年間累計報告記事。季節性の公衆衛生当局による定期的な注意喚起であり、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低いが、重症例・死亡例の継続的発生があるため動向を注視すべき。

article.articleHeadline: Ituri : 18 personnes décédées d'Ebola enterrées en l'espace de 24 heures à Biakato
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ituri: 18 people who died of Ebola buried within 24 hours in Biakato.
article.articleSummary: 18 Ebola deaths were buried within 24 hours in Biakato, capital of Babila-Babombi chiefdom, Mambasa, Ituri, on Oct 4, 2026, highlighting Biakato as a major outbreak hotspot. In Mahagi, Ituri, 24 deaths among 50 confirmed Ebola cases were recorded by Oct 2, 2026, since the outbreak declaration. Logistical difficulties hinder response, including a need for fuel for vehicles and an ambulance. The World Health Organization is deploying a rapid-response team to Mambasa and Mandima, with UNICEF and World Food Programme support delivering essential medicines and PPE to Mandima to reinforce care and prevention. Health authorities call for vigilance, regular handwashing, rapid symptom reporting, and cooperation, while avoiding rumors and relying on official sources. Nationally, the Congo Ebola outbreak has 4,018 deaths from 8,300 confirmed cases in seven provinces (Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Bas-Uele, Haut-Uele, Tshopo, Sud-Ubangi); 2,162 recoveries, 842 in isolation or hospital; 80.6% contact follow-up.

triage.headline_ja: イツリ州：ビアカトで24時間以内にエボラで死亡した18人が埋葬される
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で進行中の大規模エボラ出血熱アウトブレイク（7州にわたり確認症例8,300件、死亡4,018件）であり、重症度・拡大リスクともに高く、国際機関（WHO、UNICEF、WFP）が対応支援を行っている。
triage.notes: コンゴ民主共和国で継続中の大規模エボラ出血熱アウトブレイク。イツリ州ビアカト及びマハギで多数の死亡例が報告され、WHO・UNICEF・WFPが物資・人員支援を展開中。燃料不足や救急車不足など対応上の課題あり。全国で致死率約48%と非常に高い。

locations.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

article.articleHeadline: Mosquitos da dengue avançam pelo planeta e aumentam casos da doença
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue-carrying mosquitoes spread across the globe and increase dengue cases.
article.articleSummary: Dengue-carrying Aedes mosquitoes—A. aegypti and A. albopictus—are expanding beyond tropical zones. The WHO European Office notes the tiger mosquito is present in 31 countries, a 55% increase over seven years, heightening surveillance and vector control needs in spring and summer. In the United States, dengue has arrived in Florida, which accounts for 485 of 2,145 confirmed cases this year; Orange County issued its first mosquito-borne disease alert in 15 years. California’s Debug program has proposed releasing 32 million Wolbachia-infected, non-transmitting A. aegypti. In Brazil, Wolbachia reduced dengue by about 90% in Niterói. Europe already shows local transmission in Croatia, France, Italy, Spain, and Portugal per ECDC; London reports cases in the metro area. Climate warming drives expansion, with Copernicus noting widespread thermal stress. Brazil’s dengue rose from 80 cases in 2018 in Rio Grande do Sul to 2.4k this year; 2024–2025 were worse, and spread remains a public health concern.

triage.headline_ja: デング熱を媒介する蚊が世界中に拡大し、デング熱症例が増加
triage.triage_reason: ヒトスジシマカ等の媒介蚊の生息域拡大とブラジル（リオグランデドスル州）での症例急増（2018年80件→今年2400件）が確認され、IHR基準の複数（深刻性・異常性・国際拡大）に該当するため。
triage.notes: 記事はデング熱媒介蚊（ヒトスジシマカ等）の世界的な分布拡大を扱う広範なトレンド記事で、米国・欧州各国の情報も含むが対象国リストに該当するのはブラジルのみ。ブラジルではリオグランデドスル州での症例急増（2018年80件→2026年2400件）とニテロイ市でのウォルバキア法による90%減少成功例が記載されており、これらは具体的な公衆衛生上の懸念として注視すべき。重症度・管理可能性については記事内に具体的記載なく不明。

article.articleHeadline: Rusiyada vəba xəstəliyinin aşkarlandığı, 1 nəfərin öldüyü, xəstəxanalarda 3 həftəlik karantin elan edildiyi barədə məlumat yayılıb
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Reports have emerged that plague has been detected in Russia, one person has died, and a three-week quarantine has been announced in hospitals.
article.articleSummary: Plague detected in Irkutsk Oblast, Russia, with one death and a three-week hospital quarantine. Darya Shipilova, 28, a laboratory technician at the Plague Institute, died shortly after admission on Sept 29; theories vary whether she contracted pneumonic plague after returning from Thailand or due to an accidental breach of a test tube containing the pathogen. On Oct 4, Baykal's People reported three-week quarantines across Irkutsk hospitals, including City Clinical Hospitals No. 1, 3, and 10, plus Ivano-Matreninskaya Children’s Hospital; a maternity hospital was reportedly quarantined as well. Rospotrebnadzor says the sanitary-epidemiological situation is stable, with no pathogens linked to the deceased’s occupation and no incidents of pathogens at the Plague Institute. Irkutsk authorities have not confirmed a plague case or death. Oct 2–3 actions included a meeting between the regional governor and Anna Popova, and mask mandates at Selexov Aluminum Plant. By Oct 2, 197 contacts had been quarantined, none showing symptoms.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアでペスト感染が確認され、1人が死亡、病院で3週間の隔離が発表されたとの情報が流れた
triage.triage_reason: ロシア・イルクーツク州でペスト（肺ペストの可能性）による死亡例が報告され、複数病院で隔離措置が取られているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当し、フルリスク評価が必要と判断した。
triage.notes: 発生地はロシア・イルクーツク州であり、対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsは空とした。タイは死亡者の渡航歴として言及されているのみで、発生国ではない。ロシア当局は感染例・死亡例を公式には確認していない点に留意。

article.articleHeadline: Agenda-setting relations between Chinese state media reports and public social media posts: focusing on COVID-19
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 coverage in China shows divergent agenda patterns for state media (People’s Daily) versus social media (Weibo) across four periods. In the imminent period, People’s Daily linked infection-status updates with official directives and Wuhan-related notifications, while Weibo centered on exploratory signals and uncertainty. In the current period, People’s Daily shifted toward crisis management and resource mobilization at the national level; Weibo focused on Wuhan’s outbreak, patient treatment, and regional spread. In the critical period, People’s Daily integrated international coordination, interregional experience sharing, and standardized data releases, producing a coherent governance-oriented network; Weibo emphasized official statistics, press briefings, suspected-case responses, and overseas developments, maintaining information transmission. During the dormant period, People’s Daily broadened to global response, economic consequences, and post-outbreak policy objectives, whereas Weibo remained oriented to routine testing and provincial updates. As of 2026-10-05, comparative analysis highlights governance-embedded versus monitoring-oriented infection-status agendas across the COVID-19 issue cycle.

triage.headline_ja: 中国国営メディア報道とソーシャルメディア投稿のアジェンダセッティング関係：COVID-19に焦点を当てて
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はCOVID-19に関する学術的なメディア言説分析であり、新規の感染症発生や公衆衛生上のイベントを報告するものではない。
triage.notes: 本記事は2019-2020年のCOVID-19流行期における中国メディア報道とSNS投稿の比較研究論文であり、新規の感染症事例報告ではないため、トリアージ対象外。

article.articleHeadline: Sri Lanka Reports 860 New HIV Infections; Among 21 Countries With Rising HIV Cases
article.articleSummary: Sri Lanka reports 860 new HIV infections in the past year, bringing total HIV-positive individuals to 7,403. The National STD/AIDS Control Programme says 1,217,419 people were tested by end of Q4 last year, with a detection rate of 0.07%. In the fourth quarter, the male-to-female ratio among new infections was 7:1. Youth aged 15–24 accounted for new cases, while adult prevalence remains 0.1%. Authorities emphasize early testing and treatment to improve outcomes. The rise in Sri Lanka’s HIV cases mirrors a global trend, with UNAIDS noting increases in 21 countries in 2025, including Afghanistan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Kenya, Sudan, Brazil, Pakistan, Yemen, Egypt, Senegal and the Philippines.

triage.headline_ja: スリランカで860人の新規HIV感染を報告、HIV感染増加の21カ国の一つに

article.articleHeadline: Bird Flu Detected in Andhra Pradesh's Anantapur, around 2,500 Chickens Die
article.articleSummary: Bird flu confirmed in Anantapur district, Andhra Pradesh, at Sudarampuram village, Bukkarayasamudram mandal, after about 2,500 chickens died suddenly at a poultry farm over several days. Samples were sent to NIHSAD, Bhopal, which confirmed the bird flu virus. A 10-kilometre surveillance zone has been declared around Sudarampuram; the farm and surrounding area are under official monitoring. A joint inspection by Animal Husbandry, Health, Revenue, and Police departments is in progress, with measures to prevent spread and maintain routine movement controls on poultry within the area. Residents are urged to avoid disposing of dead chickens or poultry waste in open areas to reduce transmission risk and to follow precautionary guidelines. The article does not report any human cases. Date: 5 October 2026. Authorities continue surveillance and containment efforts to curb further transmission within Anantapur.

triage.headline_ja: アンドラプラデシュ州アナンタプールで鳥インフルエンザ確認、約2,500羽の鶏が死亡

triage.notes: 人感染例は報告されておらず、家禽農場における局地的な発生であり、当局により10km監視圏の設定と移動制限等の封じ込め対応が実施されている。ウイルス株（H5N1等）の詳細は記事に記載なし。

article.articleHeadline: Suspected Plague Death In Russia Sparks Concerns, WHO Map Shows Countries Hit By Disease; Is India Covered
article.articleSummary: 28-year-old laboratory technician Darya Shipilova died in the Irkutsk region of Siberia from a suspected pneumonic plague, though Russian officials have not confirmed plague as the cause; the regional governor described the illness as pneumonia of unknown origin. About 200 contacts in Irkutsk have been placed under observation. Shipilova worked at the Anti-Plague Research Institute in Shelekhov; media reports say exposure may have occurred after a broken test tube, though this is unverified. The incident is described as suspected plague-related rather than a confirmed outbreak. WHO notes plague is caused by Yersinia pestis and can spread by fleas, contact with infected tissues, or inhalation of respiratory particles. The WHO plague map (2019–2025) lists Congo, Madagascar, Kenya, Uganda, China, Mongolia as having reported human cases; India is not listed. The US State Department says it is monitoring unverified reports of a fatal pneumonic plague case in Russia and urges disclosure.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアでペスト感染による死亡疑い事例が発生、WHOの地図は流行国を示す－インドは含まれるか
triage.triage_reason: ロシア・シベリアの研究所関連者が肺ペスト疑いで死亡し約200人が観察下に置かれるなど、公衆衛生上深刻かつ異常な事案であり、IHR基準の複数該当が見込まれるためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 本事例はロシア（シベリア・イルクーツク州）で発生した疑いペスト死亡例であり、対象国リスト（Zambia, Philippines, Thailand, Ghana, DRC, Brazil, Indonesia, China, Myanmar, Vietnam, India）には該当しない。記事中のDRC・China・India等はWHOの過去の流行国マップの参考情報であり、実際の発生国ではないため verified_locations には含めない。

article.articleHeadline: В России распространилась информация о выявлении чумы, смерти одного человека и введении трехнедельного карантина в больницах
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In Russia, information has spread about the detection of plague, the death of one person, and the introduction of a three-week quarantine in hospitals.
article.articleSummary: Plague concerns in Irkutsk Oblast, Russia, after the death of 28-year-old Darya Shipilova, a lab worker at the Anti-Plague Institute in Shelekhov. Shipilova was hospitalized September 29 and died two days later. Media propose two scenarios: she contracted pneumonia of unknown etiology potentially linked to plague after returning from Thailand, or she allegedly broke a vial of a plague agent. By October 4, Irkutsk hospitals No. 1, No. 3, No. 10, and the Ivan-Matreninskaya Children’s Hospital were placed under a three-week quarantine, with reports of additional maternity hospital quarantine. Rospotrebnadzor said the sanitary-epidemiological situation is stable, noting no organisms tied to the institute and no pathogenic incidents. Government officials discussed a suspicious case with Anna Popova on October 2. Contact tracing began; about 197 people were quarantined and tested, with no symptoms detected.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアでペスト発生の情報が拡散、1名死亡、病院で3週間の検疫導入
triage.triage_reason: ペスト研究所勤務者の死亡と複数病院の検疫導入という異常事態が報じられ、社会的関心も高まっているため、WPRO基準（異常性・重症度・流行可能性）に複数該当する。

article.articleHeadline: Karantina Kalbar Cegah Masuknya Rabies dari Perbatasan
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: West Kalimantan quarantine prevents rabies from entering from the border.
article.articleSummary: On 5 October 2026, West Kalimantan Animal, Fish and Plant Quarantine Service (BKHIT) prevented potential rabies entry at the border by offering free veterinary health checks at two border posts, PLBN Nanga Badau (Kapuas Hulu) and PLBN Aruk (Sambas). At Nanga Badau, 35 animals were examined (32 cats, 2 dogs, 1 monkey); similar services were provided to residents’ pets at Aruk. After comprehensive health assessments, eligible animals received vaccination. The activity coincides with World Rabies Day and the quarantine service’s 149th anniversary, aiming to strengthen rabies prevention in high-mobility border zones. Authorities also educated the public on quarantine duties and cross-border movement procedures for animals, fish, and plants, emphasizing reporting obligations to prevent entry, spread of pests, and diseases across borders.

triage.headline_ja: 西カリマンタン検疫、国境からの狂犬病侵入を防止

article.articleHeadline: Pest-Todesfall in Russland: Jetzt blickt auch Washington nach Sibirien
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Plague death in Russia: Washington now eyes Siberia.
article.articleSummary: As of 5 October 2026, a suspected death from pneumonic plague has drawn attention in Russia's Irkutsk region. A 28-year-old laboratory technician at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute—where live plague agents are studied—allegedly died, though authorities have not officially confirmed the cause. The United States reportedly monitors the case due to possible human-to-human transmission of pneumonic plague. Approximately 200 contacts in the region are under medical observation, and a hospital department in Schelechow, west of Irkutsk, has been sealed off. How the technician contracted the disease remains unclear; local media cite a possible laboratory accident (a broken vial), but this is unconfirmed. A Thailand travel link is another unverified theory. No additional infections have been reported in Russia, leaving open whether this is an isolated incident.

article.articleHeadline: ஆய்வகத்திலிருந்து பரவிய கொடூர பாக்டீரியா.. இளம் விஞ்ஞானி அதிர்ச்சி மரணம்! மீண்டும் கோவிட் பெருந்தொற்றா?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Deadly bacteria spreading from the lab.. A young scientist's shocking death! Another huge COVID outbreak?

More than 200 contacts and hospital staff exposed to her are under intensive medical surveillance and isolation. All major public events in Irkutsk have been canceled; panic-driven shortages of plague medications are reported. Globally, fear rises with parallels drawn to the COVID-19 pandemic, and speculation that a Wuhan, China laboratory may be a source; the White House says authorities are monitoring the situation.

triage.headline_ja: 研究所から流出した恐ろしい細菌…若い科学者が衝撃死！再びコロナ級のパンデミックか？

article.articleHeadline: Russian lab worker dies of suspected plague as 200 enter medical observation
article.articleSummary: One death in Irkutsk, Russia: a 28-year-old lab worker at an anti-plague institute may have contracted pneumonic plague. Authorities have not confirmed the cause; pneumonia of unknown etiology is cited. Nearly 200 people who were in contact are under precautionary medical observation, and the inpatient facility where she was treated has been quarantined. Pneumonic plague is highly contagious and can trigger severe epidemics, per WHO, though experts say person-to-person spread is unlikely to fuel a large outbreak. The sanitary-epidemiological situation in the Irkutsk region and the cities of Irkutsk and Shelekhov is described as stable. The U.S. State Department and CDC are monitoring; no confirmation of laboratory confirmation yet. Globally, 2019–2025 saw more than 3,800 suspected plague cases reported to WHO from 10 countries, with 423 deaths, mainly in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Madagascar.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアの研究所職員がペスト疑いで死亡、200人が経過観察下に

article.articleHeadline: Bupati Demak pastikan belum ada laporan kasus influenza tipe A
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Demak Regent confirms there have been no reports of influenza type A cases.
article.articleSummary: As of 5 October 2026, Demak Regency, Central Java, Indonesia, has not reported any influenza type A cases. Bupati Demak Eisti'anah and Kepala Dinas Kesehatan Ali Maimun urged continued vigilance and preventive measures, including handwashing, masking when sick, and reducing contact with others. They instructed residents with flu-like symptoms to seek medical assessment at health facilities, and highlighted ongoing prevention and surveillance at Puskesmas. Ali Maimun added that no new influenza strain has been detected in the area. Influenza is caused by viruses and, with a healthy immune system, symptoms typically resolve in about a week. Allergies and dusty environments can trigger flu-like symptoms. Public health guidance emphasizes clean living (PHBS), masking during illness, avoiding unnecessary crowds, and adequate rest.

article.articleHeadline: रशियात तयार होत होता कोरोनासारखाच घातक विषाणू?; सायबेरियातील लॅबमधील स्फोटानंतर जगभरात संतापाची लाट
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Was a deadly virus similar to coronavirus being developed in Russia?; A wave of outrage worldwide after a Siberian lab explosion.

Amid online speculation about a coronavirus-like pathogen or a 'second Wuhan,' Russian authorities said no infection has been detected and the pneumonia suffered by the deceased was of unknown origin. Tests on people exposed to the lab were negative. The incident highlighted the risk of handling high-risk pathogens, though officials maintained that no pathogen outbreak occurred and containment measures were in place.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアでコロナウイルスに似た致命的なウイルスが開発されていたのか？；シベリアの研究所爆発後、世界中で怒りの波

article.articleHeadline: அச்சுறுத்தும் டெங்கு காய்ச்சல்.. பாதுகாத்துக்கொள்வது எப்படி?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Threatening Dengue Fever.. How to Protect Yourself?
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever remains a major concern in Tamil Nadu’s Chennai Corporation area, with 4,592 dengue infections reported this year, alongside typhoid and other viral fevers. Emergency measures and dedicated medical camps aim to curb spread and provide timely care, contributing to a gradual decline in cases. Most patients are managing illness at home; only about 5–10% require intensive medical supervision. Public vigilance is crucial to prevent transmission, since the Aedes aegypti mosquito can bite during the day and spread the infection to others if not controlled. Protective actions include covering arms and legs, using safe repellents, keeping doors and windows screened, and employing mosquito coils or electric devices when mosquitoes are prevalent. If dengue is present nearby, cleaning and maintaining surroundings is essential; eliminating standing water in the neighborhood reduces risk for all residents.

triage.headline_ja: 脅威となるデング熱…どうやって自分を守るか?
triage.triage_reason: タミル・ナードゥ州チェンナイでデング熱4,592例の報告があるが、季節性のありふれた流行で既に減少傾向にあり、公衆衛生上の啓発記事の性格が強いため、フルRRAに進めるほどの異常性・国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: インド・タミル・ナードゥ州（チェンナイ）における季節性デング熱・腸チフスに関する予防啓発記事。症例数は減少傾向であり、国際的な懸念は低い。

article.articleHeadline: Russia Plague Scare: From Symptoms To Spread, How Dangerous It Is And Could It Be Another Covid?
article.articleSummary: In Siberia, a 28-year-old laboratory worker at an anti-plague research institute died after severe pneumonia; a suspected pneumonic plague case prompted international attention, with nearly 200 close contacts placed under medical observation. Russia's Rospotrebnadzor has not officially confirmed plague and says expanded testing found no microorganisms linked to her professional activities; the United States and other agencies are monitoring as of 2026-10-05. Plague is caused by Yersinia pestis and remains endemic in parts of Africa, Asia and the Americas, with most recent cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Madagascar. There are three forms: bubonic, septicaemic, and pneumonic—the latter is the only form that transmits between people. Pneumonic plague presents with fever, headache, weakness, rapidly progressing pneumonia, shortness of breath, chest pain, and a cough producing bloody or watery mucus; incubation can be as short as 24 hours. Untreated pneumonic plague can be fatal within 18–24 hours, but antibiotics and early treatment save lives. A single case does not indicate a COVID-like pandemic.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアのペスト警戒:症状から拡散まで、その危険性と新型コロナの再来となり得るか

article.articleHeadline: Imponen la cuarentena en varios hospitales de Siberia por sospecha de casos de peste pulmonar
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Quarantine imposed in several hospitals in Siberia amid suspected pneumonic plague cases.
article.articleSummary: Quarantine imposed in at least four hospitals in the Irkutsk region, Siberia, amid suspected pneumonic plague cases. Authorities have not confirmed pneumonic plague; diagnosis described as pneumonia of undetermined etiology in official channels. Quarantines span up to three weeks and include a pediatric hospital; visits restricted and family access prohibited. Governor Igor Kobzev convened an emergency meeting with broad public health actions, including contact tracing and medical observation; as of 2026-10-05, no symptomatic cases and all tests negative. A 28-year-old woman, an employee at the Institute of Plague Research of Irkutsk and the Far East, died last week in Shelekhov, prompting questions about infection source. Two possible origins cited: recent travel to Thailand or an accidental lab breach with pathogens at the institute. Rospotrebnadzor reports no pathogen-related emergencies at the institute.

triage.headline_ja: シベリアの複数の病院で肺ペスト疑い例により検疫措置

article.articleHeadline: Qué es la peste neumónica, cómo se transmite y por qué casi 200 personas están en cuarentena en Rusia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: What is pneumonic plague, how is it transmitted, and why nearly 200 people are in quarantine in Russia.
article.articleSummary: Pneumonic plague detected in Russia, causing the death of a worker at the Irkutsk Institute for Plague Research and prompting the quarantine of nearly 200 people. Causative agent is Yersinia pestis; transmission occurs via infected fleas and, in the pneumonic form, through respiratory droplets between people. WHO warns pneumonic plague is the most severe form and can spread rapidly; incubation may be as short as 24 hours, underscoring the need for swift case identification and contact tracing. Diagnosis is laboratory-confirmed by detecting Y. pestis in blood, sputum, or bubo material; treatment relies on antibiotics, with early therapy markedly improving prognosis. Isolation, contact surveillance, and antibiotic treatment are key for suspected cases. The disease persists in animal reservoirs in parts of Africa, Asia, and the Americas; historically affected countries include Madagascar, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Peru. Ongoing risk hinges on timely diagnosis and public health response, rather than a new Black Death.

triage.headline_ja: 肺ペストとは何か、どのように感染し、なぜロシアで約200人が隔離されているのか

article.articleHeadline: 猴痘｜8月起本地個案顯著上升 歐家榮：部分以交友程式尋性伴難追蹤
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Monkeypox | Local cases have risen significantly since August; Ou Ka-wing: Some people are using dating apps to find sexual partners, making contact tracing difficult.
article.articleSummary: Monkeypox outbreak in Hong Kong has risen sharply since August 2026, with 29 cases this year: 22 locally acquired and 7 imported; 20 new cases have been reported since August. Dr. Ou Ka-wing, Director of the CHP Infectious Disease Office, notes that 60% of infections involve men who have sex with men using dating apps to find casual partners, complicating contact tracing as many cannot provide partner contacts or sources. No clear epidemiological links among cases have been identified; authorities believe transmission is ongoing within a small network. Of the 20 recent cases, 15 are local and 5 imported; all patients are men who have sex with men and report high-risk sexual behavior, including with strangers, multiple partners, or not using condoms. In response, the CHP has intensified public health messaging on social media and dating apps, expanded vaccination for high-risk groups, and opened an additional monkeypox vaccination center at the CHP building; citizens are urged to retain partner contact details for tracing.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Possible outbreak of pneumonic plague in a hospital in Siberia following the suspicious death of a laboratory technician in Irkutsk.
article.articleSummary: On 2026-10-05, reports of a possible pneumonic plague outbreak emerged after the suspicious death of Darya S., a laboratory technician at Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute in Irkutsk, Siberia. A hospital in Sholkhov near Irkutsk fully quarantined its inpatient department, with about 197–200 people under medical surveillance and roughly 189 hospitalized. Health authorities have not formally confirmed plague; narratives diverge whether the deceased had returned from Thailand or was exposed while handling live plague bacteria at the institute, with no independent verification. Investigations were opened into potential safety-regulation violations. Governor Igor Kobzov held a special health and epidemiology meeting; all public events in Irkutsk were canceled, and Anna Popova, head of Russia’s health watchdog, traveled to the region. Contacts identified are under monitoring; current tests among them are negative. Plague is rare but antibiotic-treatable; the last known Russian case was in 2016, a 10-year-old in Altai Republic.

article.articleHeadline: Imponen cuarentena en varios hospitales de Siberia por sospecha de peste pulmonar
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Quarantine imposed in several hospitals in Siberia due to suspected pneumonic plague.
article.articleSummary: Quarantine imposed in several hospitals in the Irkutsk region of Siberia amid a suspected pneumonic plague outbreak. Liudi Baikala reported that at least four facilities, including a pediatric hospital, have quarantines of up to three weeks, with strict visitation bans and restricted patient access. Authorities have not publicly confirmed pneumonic plague; no official document lists that diagnosis. Governor Igor Kobzev convened an emergency meeting after a suspected contagion case, with all contacts under medical observation; to date, none show symptoms and all tests are negative. Meduza cites the death of a 28-year-old woman who worked at the Institute of Plague Research of Irkutsk and the Far East, in Shélejov, last week; the cause is listed by some sources as pneumonia of unknown etiology. Rospotrebnadzor notes no emergencies at the institute; two infection-source possibilities: Thailand infection or an accidental lab tube break. No confirmed plague cases.

triage.triage_reason: 肺ペスト疑いで複数病院が隔離措置、関連と疑われる死亡例も出ており、IHR基準（深刻性・異常性）に複数該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Karantina Kalimantan Barat cegah masuknya rabies dari perbatasan
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: West Kalimantan quarantine prevents the entry of rabies from the border.
article.articleSummary: Rabies prevention efforts by West Kalimantan’s Animal, Fish, and Plant Quarantine Agency (BKHIT Kalbar) at two border posts, PLBN Nanga Badau (Kapuas Hulu) and PLBN Aruk (Sambas). Free animal health checks were conducted, with 35 animals served at Nanga Badau (32 cats, 2 dogs, 1 monkey); a similar service extended to residents’ pets at Aruk. Health checks precede vaccination for animals meeting eligibility, strengthening rabies control amid high cross-border mobility. Led by Ferdi, head of Kalbar quarantine, the initiative also provides education on quarantine duties and movement procedures for cross-border animal, fish, and plant commodities, and reminds the public to report border-crossing items to prevent pests and diseases. Coincides with World Rabies Day (theme “Stronger Together”) and the quarantine agency’s 149th anniversary, highlighting community-based vaccine and surveillance efforts at the border.

article.articleHeadline: Influenza A Merebak, Dokter Larang Sembarangan Minum Antibiotik
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Influenza A Spreads, Doctors Ban Indiscriminate Use of Antibiotics.
article.articleSummary: As of 5 October 2026, influenza A cases are rising in several regions of Indonesia, including Jakarta. Dr. Edwin Nugroho Njoto emphasizes recognizing influenza symptoms and avoiding unsanctioned antibiotic use. Influenza A is caused by the influenza virus and spreads mainly through respiratory droplets from coughing or sneezing, with higher risk for the elderly, children, pregnant women, and individuals with diabetes or kidney disease. Common symptoms include runny nose, cough, fever, and sore throat; warning signs include reduced appetite and shortness of breath. Antibiotics do not treat influenza and should only be used if a bacterial secondary infection is confirmed. Prevention includes rest, hydration, nutritious meals, regular activity, handwashing, mask-wearing when sick, proper cough etiquette, and annual influenza vaccination, especially for high-risk groups.

article.articleHeadline: 30 students fall ill after educational trip in Jharkhands Khunti
article.articleSummary: At least 30 students from PM Shri High School, Tilmi, in Jharkhand’s Khunti district fell ill after a 3 October school outing to a gurukul at Dodma and Rani Falls in Torpa block. Symptoms include vomiting, loose motions, high fever and stomach pain; several have been admitted to Karra Community Health Centre and are in stable condition. Most affected are from Tilmi village, with a few from Masko and Barwadag. Officials say the illness could be linked to the trip, noting meals were cooked by students and some ate from roadside stalls, but no confirmed tainted food or infection source yet. Health teams have been deployed to Tilmi, Masko, and Barwadag; door-to-door checks and heightened surveillance are in place. The district hospital is on alert as medical and epidemiological investigations continue to establish the cause.

article.articleHeadline: 뜨거워지는 지구, '모기 지도' 바꾼다...온대 지방 노리는 뎅기열 [달콤한 사이언스]
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The warming Earth is changing the 'mosquito map'... Dengue fever targeting temperate regions [Sweet Science].
article.articleSummary: Warming climate and altered precipitation expand conditions favorable to mosquitoes, but non-climate factors shape malaria and dengue differently. A Monash University-led study in Science Advances (Oct 3) finds dengue is spreading toward temperate regions, while malaria remains in long-term decline yet shows rising risk in some areas. Dengue climate suitability increases for Aedes aegypti by 12% and Aedes albopictus by 49%, with transmission now reported in Brazil, Asia–Pacific, the US South, and mainland France. Malaria suitability grows only about 2%. Dengue’s spread is amplified by urbanization and artificial containers; its vector is day-biting, reducing bed-net effectiveness and there is no widely effective cure. Malaria control—antimalarials, insecticide-treated nets, indoor spraying—reduced incidence by 36% and deaths by 60% amid funding growth from $1.5B to $4.3B (2000–2016). The urban-adapted Anopheles stephensi is spreading to Djibouti, Ethiopia, and the Horn of Africa. New tools include the four-valent dengue vaccine Qudenga and Wolbachia-infected mosquitoes; climate mitigation remains essential.

triage.headline_ja: 温暖化する地球、「蚊の地図」を変える…温帯地方を狙うデング熱 [달콤한 사이언스]
triage.triage_reason: 特定の国・地域における急性アウトブレイクの報告ではなく、気候変動とマラリア・デング熱媒介蚊の分布変化に関する学術研究（Science Advances誌）を紹介する一般科学記事であるため、公衆衛生上の緊急対応を要するシグナルとは言えない。
triage.notes: 記事は特定の急性アウトブレイクではなく、気候変動による蚊媒介感染症の分布変化に関する学術研究の紹介記事。Brazilは「デング熱の伝播が現在報告されている地域」として言及されているため対象国として含めたが、具体的な発生状況の詳細はない。France, US(Missouri), Djibouti, Ethiopiaは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Qué es la peste neumónica, cómo se transmite y por qué casi 200 personas están en cuarentena en Rusia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: What is pneumonic plague, how is it transmitted, and why nearly 200 people are in quarantine in Russia.
article.articleSummary: Pneumonic plague case detected in Russia, resulting in the death of a worker at the Irkutsk Institute of Plague Research; about 200 people are quarantined in connection with the exposure. Caused by Yersinia pestis, plague transmits to humans via fleas; the pneumonic form spreads between people through respiratory droplets. The WHO notes pneumonic plague is the most severe and can rapidly progress; incubation can be as short as 24 hours. Diagnosis is through laboratory tests identifying Y. pestis in blood, sputum, or bubal material. Treatment is through antibiotics, with early treatment markedly improving prognosis. Isolation, contact tracing, and antibiotic therapy are applied for suspected cases. While plague remains present globally, most cases occur in Africa, Asia, and the Americas, historically impacting Madagascar, the Democratic Republic of Congo, and Peru; this is not an indication of a new Black Death.

article.articleHeadline: छोटे बच्चों में मेनिनजाइटिस का खतरा, इलाज में न करें जरा भी देरी; जान जाने तक खतरा - agra meningitis risk in children dont delay treatment
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Meningitis risk in young children; do not delay treatment even for a moment; risk of death - Agra
article.articleSummary: Agra, 2026-10-05 — Viral meningitis in children and TB-related meningitis are rising, with affected youngsters admitted in government and private hospitals in serious condition. On Meningitis Day, doctors at SN Medical College & Hospital in Agra urged timely diagnosis and treatment to prevent deaths. Emergency department screenings show about 5% of children presenting with loss of consciousness have meningitis. Pediatrician Dr. Neeraj Yadav explains that in children under five, viral and bacterial infections, along with brain coverings inflammation, reduce brain oxygen and trigger seizures, high fever, headache, vomiting, and sometimes unconsciousness. Delayed treatment can be fatal; survivors may suffer paralysis, and TB meningitis increases this risk. Preventive steps include vaccinations (BCG, meningococcal, Haemophilus influenzae type b, and pneumococcal), hygiene, and nutritious meals to strengthen immunity. Seek immediate medical care for fever with seizures or altered consciousness.

article.articleHeadline: Rusijoje užfiksuota mirtis nuo maro: įvestas karantinas
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Death from plague recorded in Russia: quarantine imposed.
article.articleSummary: Death from pneumonic plague reported in Russia’s Irkutsk region, prompting a three-week quarantine across Irkutsk City Clinical Hospital Nos. 1, 3 and 10 and the Ivano-Matreninska Children’s Hospital. In Shelekhov, 28-year-old Darja Shipilova, a hospital patient and laboratory technician at the Plague Control Institute, died after admission in late September. Two competing narratives emerged: she had returned from Thailand with pneumonic plague, or she accidentally shattered a vial containing plague agent; authorities say no pathogen related to her work was found in her body and the institute reports no incidents. The health service characterizes the situation as stable and has implemented special measures, including a mask mandate at the Irkutsk Aluminum Plant. About 197 people were quarantined in Shelekhov, with none developing symptoms. Officials have engaged with federal authorities; statements over whether the patient visited Buryatia were later revised to a possible plague death.

article.articleHeadline: Socioeconomic vulnerability associated with schistosomiasis in indigenous communities of southern Brazil
article.articleSummary: Schistosomiasis, a snail-borne neglected tropical disease caused by Schistosoma mansoni, was evaluated in six indigenous communities in southern Brazil (n=412) and four in southeastern Brazil (n=301). Among 713 individuals, overall seropositivity for anti-S. mansoni antibodies (IgM and/or IgG) was 5.3% (38/713; 95% CI 3.9–7.2). Seroprevalence was 5.8% in the southern region (24/412) and 4.7% in the southeastern region (14/301), with no statistical difference between regions. Among seropositive individuals, IgM predominated (33/38; 86.8%) versus IgG (10/38; 26.3%), suggesting recent infection. Univariate associations included drinking river water and open-pit fecal disposal; however, final logistic regression retained community location/characteristic as the associated variable. The findings support ongoing schistosomiasis surveillance in low-endemic areas, particularly in indigenous communities serving as environmental sentinels of pathogen distribution.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Want to avoid the risk of dengue and malaria before Durga Puja? Make five changes at home first to prevent mosquito bites.
article.articleSummary: On 2026-10-05, a Bangla article urges households to implement five changes to reduce dengue, malaria, and chikungunya risks ahead of Durga Puja. As the monsoon lingers into autumn, mosquito-borne infections can surge, making preventive measures essential. Implement these steps: 1) Keep windows closed at dawn as well as dusk and install window nets; inspect nets for holes. 2) Run ceiling fans in the evening and maintain good indoor airflow; burn incense to deter mosquitoes. 3) Eliminate standing water around the home; remove stagnant water from rooftops, gardens, pots, tubs, or open containers after rain. 4) Be cautious with indoor plants and floral arrangements; avoid water accumulation at plant bases or in vases and change water regularly. 5) Do not accumulate garbage; empty trash bins daily and keep the area clean to reduce mosquito breeding.

article.articleHeadline: وزير الصحة في الكونغو الديمقراطية: انخفاض ملحوظ في حالات الإصابة الجديدة بفيروس إيبولا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Minister of Health in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: notable decline in new Ebola virus infection cases.
article.articleSummary: As of 5 October 2026, the Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo shows a notable decline in new infections, according to Health Minister Samuel Roger Kamba. In a press briefing cited by All Africa, he said epidemiological indicators indicate the worst is over and authorities have regained control, shifting from passive surveillance to proactive outbreak management. Transmission is now concentrated in a limited number of health zones; among 63 monitored zones, 12 have reported no new cases for more than 42 days, and eight have had no cases for 22–42 days. Officials report a gradual decrease in active outbreak foci, with some areas still reporting cases but at declining levels. The minister urged partners to improve transparency in managing funds donated for the Ebola response. The report provides no specific case counts or laboratory confirmation details.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国保健相:エボラウイルスの新規感染例が顕著に減少

triage.notes: 記事は既存のエボラ流行の進捗報告であり、新規感染例は減少傾向にあるが、依然として複数の保健区域で感染が継続しており、資金管理の透明性向上を求める声が出ている。具体的な症例数や検査確認情報は記載なし。

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ministry of Health: Ebola tests for the suspected case came back negative.
article.articleSummary: As of 5 October 2026, Ebola tests for a person admitted to a hospital in Israel with suspected infection after returning from the Democratic Republic of Congo were negative. The Ministry noted the tests were conducted under professional procedures and internationally accepted guidelines for high-risk communicable diseases. There has been no confirmed Ebola case in Israel to date. The suspicion arose after symptoms appeared following the Congo return, prior to hospital admission and testing under suspected-case protocols. The Ministry reminded that Ebola is not airborne and spreads through direct contact with a symptomatic patient, or through contact with blood, bodily fluids, or secretions. It pledged ongoing briefings to the public and medical teams as updates arise.

article.articleHeadline: Ärzte ohne Grenzen: Ebola-Ausbruch noch nicht unter Kontrolle - Deutsches Ärzteblatt
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Doctors Without Borders: Ebola outbreak not yet under control - German Medical Journal
article.articleSummary: Outbreak of Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo is not yet under control, driven by Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV). Seven health zones are affected, with Kisangani in the northeast as a focal point; analysts warn that Kinshasa could be next. Confirmed cases exceed 8,000, with nearly 4,000 deaths and over 2,000 recoveries. The outbreak was officially acknowledged in May 2026, though it likely began months earlier. A large proportion of cases (about half) have no known epidemiological link, and contact tracing lags; lab confirmation often takes time. In Kisangani, a private clinic closed for 21 days after staff illness. Vaccination efforts include 70,000 doses of Ervebo (EBOV) and frontline immunization in Kisangani; a compassionate-use Remdesivir program is underway. Success hinges on population trust, survivor engagement, and flexible response teams.

triage.headline_ja: 国境なき医師団：エボラ出血熱の流行、いまだ制御下にない - ドイツ医師会報
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で8,000人超の感染、4,000人近い死亡を伴う大規模エボラ流行が継続しており、主要都市キンシャサへの拡大懸念や接触者追跡の遅延など複数のIHR・WPRO基準に該当するため。
triage.notes: キサンガニを中心に7つの保健ゾーンで流行が拡大中。感染者の約半数で疫学的リンク不明、ワクチン接種とRemdesivirの人道的使用プログラムが進行中。キンシャサへの拡大リスクが特に懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: Туристов из России поразил вирус Коксаки во Вьетнаме
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Russian tourists were struck by the Coxsackievirus in Vietnam.
article.articleSummary: Russian families vacationing at the Amiana Resort in Cam Ranh, Vietnam, contracted an enterovirus infection diagnosed as Coxsackievirus. An eight-month-old child developed 40°C fever, rash, and painful oral ulcers on day three after check-in; the mother soon followed with fever of 39.5°C. Local hospital confirmed Coxsackievirus; the outbreak circulates at the resort, with other families reporting similar symptoms. Hotel staff did not inform guests, offering only relocation. The families plan to fly home to Russia on Oct 8. This case fits a broader Vietnamese enterovirus surge in 2026: about 100,000 cases in Jan–Aug, 2.5 times higher than 2025, with children under five making up over 87%. Hotspots include Ho Chi Minh City, Dong Nai, Dong Thap, Tay Ninh, Lam Dong, Da Nang and Hanoi. Enterovirus 71, causing encephalitis and meningitis, accounted for 56% of confirmed cases in Ho Chi Minh City; peaks occur March–May and Sept–Dec on a three-year cycle.

triage.headline_ja: ロシア人観光客がベトナムでコクサッキーウイルスに感染
triage.triage_reason: ベトナムで2026年にエンテロウイルス感染が前年比2.5倍に急増し、EV71による脳炎例も確認されている中、外国人観光客にも感染が広がっており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルリスク評価が妥当。
triage.notes: ロシア人観光客の個別感染事例に加え、2026年のベトナム国内エンテロウイルス流行（EV71含む）が背景にあり、小児を中心に重症化例（脳炎・髄膜炎）が報告されている。渡航者への健康影響や国際的な話題性からピックアップ対象とした。

article.articleHeadline: کرونا همچنان در محدوده هشدار / کودکان در صدر موارد آنفلوانزا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: COVID-19 remains at the warning level / Children lead in influenza cases
article.articleSummary: Influenza activity rising in Iran while COVID-19 remains at high alert. In the week ending 11 Mehr, 9.3% of outpatients had influenza‑like illness and 9.7% of inpatients had severe respiratory symptoms (up from 8.1% and 10.5% the previous week). Of 203 respiratory samples tested, 2.9% were influenza‑positive; 77.5% of positives were influenza B. Children accounted for 39.3% of influenza positives (under 2 years 7.7%; 2–5 years 14.2%; 6–15 years 17.4%). Bushehr (18.7%) and Fars (11.6%) exceeded high‑alert thresholds; Khuzestan, Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari, and Kerman were below. COVID-19 positive rates fell from 17.4% in week 27 to 13.7% in week 28 but remain above high‑alert, with RV.1 circulation noted. Lab surveillance: 5,845 samples with 155 influenza positives (2.7%), influenza B dominating. WHO tracks PQ.1.6.1.1, NB.1.1.1, XFG, BA.3.2; XFG ~41% of sequences as of Aug 16; East Asia signals urge vigilance.

triage.headline_ja: コロナは依然警戒域内／インフルエンザ患者の中心は子ども
triage.triage_reason: イランにおける季節性インフルエンザおよびCOVID-19のサーベイランス報告であり、対象国（本評価リスト）には該当しない。中国への言及はWHOの変異株動向文脈のみで実発生国ではない。
triage.notes: 記事はイラン国内の季節性呼吸器疾患サーベイランスに関するもの。発生地域に含まれるShanghai Shi(中国)はWHOの変異株動向の文脈での言及であり、実際の発生国ではないため除外した。対象国リストにイランは含まれないためverified_locationsは空配列。

article.articleHeadline: Pneumonic plague suspected in Russia, no immediate threat to India: IMA expert
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-10-05, Russia is investigating a suspected case of pneumonic plague after a lab worker died of pneumonia; a laboratory containing a test tube with Yersinia pestis is cited, though the official cause of death remains unconfirmed. Indian Medical Association expert Rajeev Jayadevan says contact tracing is underway and there is no immediate threat to India. Pneumonic plague, the form affecting the lungs, can progress to death in about 24 hours, though plague has three forms: skin lesions, pneumonia, or septicemia. Symptoms can include fever, cranial discomfort, fatigue, rapid pneumonia, breathing difficulty, thoracic pain, coughing, and sometimes blood-tinged or fluid secretions. Plague is preventable with antibiotics for at‑risk contacts. Emphasizes tracing contacts to identify exposure and monitor symptoms; travel from affected Russia poses no current risk to India.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアで肺ペスト疑い、インドへの直接的な脅威はないとIMA専門家
triage.triage_reason: ロシアでの検査室職員における肺ペスト疑い死亡例は重篤かつ異常な事象であり、IHR基準2項目（深刻性・異常性）に該当するためフルリスク評価への移行が妥当。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はロシアにおける検査室関連の肺ペスト疑い死亡例であり、インドは『脅威なし』とするコメントの対象として言及されているのみで、実際の発生国ではない。ロシアは対象国リストに含まれないため、verified_locationsは空配列とした。続報でYersinia pestis感染の確定診断や感染拡大の有無を要確認。

article.articleHeadline: Why Is Plague Still A Threat? What Russia's Irkutsk Scare Reveals About The Deadly Bacteria
article.articleSummary: 28-year-old lab technician Darya Shipilova at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute died after a suspected incident involving a broken test tube containing pneumonic plague bacteria. The Sept. 25 event in Irkutsk prompted 189 people to be isolated: 114 in hospital, 63 at another facility, 12 at the institute. Irkutsk officials say contacts show no illness and lab tests are negative, though explanations vary on whether exposure came from a trip to Buryatia or the broken tube; a criminal case into health-safety violations has been opened. Authorities initially avoided the word plague, describing it as a "particularly dangerous infection." Pneumonic plague, caused by Yersinia pestis, is the most virulent form and can spread by respiratory particles; untreated, it is almost always fatal, but early antibiotics cure. Plague persists in Africa, Asia, and the Americas, with Madagascar, DRC, and Peru repeatedly affected; the US reports a few cases annually, in the rural West.

triage.headline_ja: ペストはなぜ今も脅威なのか？ロシア・イルクーツクの騒動が示す致死性細菌の実態
triage.triage_reason: 肺ペスト菌の実験室内事故により技師が死亡し189人が隔離される事態が発生。重篤な転帰と異常性（研究所での感染事故）からIHR基準を2つ満たすためフルリスク評価が妥当。
triage.notes: 本事例の発生地はロシア（イルクーツク州・ブリヤート共和国）であり、対象国リストには含まれない。記事中のマダガスカル・DRC・ペルー・米国は『ペストが依然流行している地域』としての一般的言及であり、本件の発生国ではないためverified_locationsから除外した。

article.articleHeadline: ബംഗ്ലാദേശിലെ മീസിൽസ് വ്യാപനം, കേരളത്തിലും ജാഗ്രത വേണം; വാക്സിൻ പ്രധാനം, രോഗം പകരുന്നതെങ്ങനെ ?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Spread of measles in Bangladesh; vigilance needed in Kerala as well; vaccination is the priority; how is the disease transmitted?
article.articleSummary: As of 5 October 2026, Bangladesh reports a measles outbreak with 196,418 cases and 1,125 deaths this year; 174,149 hospitalisations for measles, and 1,218 people with symptoms seeking care in the last 24 hours (1,122 admitted). In Kerala, vigilance is urged after Malappuram recorded two child deaths in September (an 18‑month‑old and a 10‑month‑old) and 103 confirmed cases; Kozhikode officials called for full immunisation. Measles spreads via respiratory droplets; incubation is 10–14 days; symptoms include fever, red rash, cough, diarrhoea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. Severe disease is most common in 6 months to 3 years. Prevention hinges on the Measles-Rubella vaccine: first dose after 9 months, second after 16 months; if a dose is missed, it can be given up to age five. Vaccination is free at government facilities. Address vaccine hesitancy; sick children should stay home, maintain hand hygiene, masking, and distancing.

triage.headline_ja: バングラデシュで麻疹が流行、ケララ州でも警戒が必要；ワクチン接種が重要、感染経路は？
triage.triage_reason: バングラデシュで麻疹による死者1,125人・症例19万件超という深刻な流行が発生し、隣接するインド・ケララ州でも小児2名が死亡し103例が確認されるなど越境拡大の兆候があるため、IHR基準を2つ以上満たしフルリスク評価が妥当と判断した。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はバングラデシュでの麻疹大流行とそれに伴うインド・ケララ州での警戒強化。バングラデシュは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めず、インド（ケララ州含む）のみを記載した。バングラデシュ側のデータ（死者1,125人等）は規模感の参考情報として記載。

article.articleHeadline: Rusijoje maras nusinešė moters gyvybę, Irkutsko ligoninėse įvestas karantinas
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In Russia, the plague claimed the life of a woman, and quarantine has been imposed in Irkutsk hospitals.
article.articleSummary: In Irkutsk region, Russia, a 28-year-old hospital patient, Darja Shipilova, who worked as a laboratory assistant at the Plague Control Institute in Shelekhov, died on Oct 1 after hospitalization on Sept 29. Reports cite possible pneumonic plague, but authorities have not confirmed the diagnosis; two versions exist—either she returned from Thailand with plague or a vial containing the agent was accidentally broken. Rospotrebnadzor says no pathogens linked to her profession were detected in her body, and the public health situation in Irkutsk region, including Irkutsk city and Shelekhov, is described as stable with special measures. On Oct 3, masks became mandatory at the Irkutsk Aluminum Plant in Shelekhov. By Oct 2, about 197 people connected to the case were quarantined; media coverage on the outbreak has been restricted as investigations proceed. No confirmed plague infections have been reported yet.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアでペストにより女性が死亡、イルクーツクの病院で検疫が実施される
triage.triage_reason: ペスト研究所職員の原因不明死亡とその後の検疫措置（197人）が発生しており、診断未確定ながら深刻性・異常性の観点からIHR基準2項目に該当するためフルRRAへの移行が妥当。
triage.notes: 発生地域としてロシア（イルクーツク州）とタイが挙げられているが、いずれも評価対象国リストに含まれていない。タイは『患者がタイから帰国した可能性がある』という未確定の仮説の一つとして言及されているのみで、実際の発生国ではないため除外。診断（肺ペストかどうか）は当局により未確認であり、続報の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Barabanki News: डेंगू व मलेरिया के मिले केस, संदिग्ध बुखार से छात्र की मौत
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Barabanki News: Cases of dengue and malaria detected, student dies from suspected fever.
article.articleSummary: Barabanki district reports a dengue case in Ramnagar and a malaria case in Masooli, with a fever outbreak spanning Mohsand (Ferozpur village), Tikaitganj, Kursi, Khijhna, Babagan and Anwari as poor sanitation drives viral fever, dengue, and malaria. As of Oct 5, 2026, a 15-year-old student from Mohsand village, Ayush (Class 8), died during treatment at a Lucknow private hospital after five days of fever; doctors attributed death to liver cirrhosis with pulmonary edema and elevated creatinine, not dengue or fever. Dozens in the area are affected by fever symptoms. Health teams distributed medicines and planned a village screening camp, with a Monday outreach to intensify care. A nodal officer, Dr. Nishant Sharma, and teams visited Ramnagar and Masooli to assess cases and provide treatment; authorities have been urged to improve sanitation to curb transmission.

triage.headline_ja: バラバンキ・ニュース：デング熱とマラリアの症例確認、原因不明の発熱で生徒死亡
triage.triage_reason: インド・バラバンキ県での局地的なデング熱・マラリア・発熱流行だが、死亡例はデング熱・マラリアとは無関係（肝硬変）とされ、季節性かつ局地的な衛生問題に起因する事例であり、国際的な拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低い。
triage.notes: Bluedotの発生地域にUganda・Indonesiaの地名が含まれるが、記事はインド・ウッタルプラデーシュ州バラバンキ県の地域ニュースであり、同名地名（Babagan等）による誤判定と考えられるため除外。死亡した生徒の死因はデング熱・マラリアではなく肝硬変とされている点に注意。

article.articleHeadline: UNMISS patrol reaches remote Ibba communities amidst heavy rains, insecurity, and growing health threats
article.articleSummary: As of 5 October 2026, UNMISS patrol reached Ibba County in Western Equatoria State, South Sudan, amid heavy rains and insecurity that have left communities isolated along the Yambio–Ibba road, a 100-km route already plagued by damaged lanes, flooding and slow travel. Attacks, vehicle ambushes and abductions heighten risk; traders note vehicles burned, goods blocked, and rising prices as supply routes via Juba–Mundri–Yambio and cross-border import from Wau/DRC have dwindled. Health concerns center on an Ebola threat in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with cross-border movement constrained. UNMISS used the visit to engage with communities, authorities and leaders on road insecurity, poor road conditions, and the Ebola threat, promising to relay concerns to authorities. Residents describe a dangerous mix of insecurity and environmental hazards that jeopardize movement and livelihoods.

triage.headline_ja: UNMISSのパトロール隊が、豪雨・治安悪化・高まる健康上の脅威の中、遠隔地イバ地域社会に到達
triage.triage_reason: DRCにおける既知のエボラ流行への言及があり、南スーダンへの越境拡大リスクが懸念されるが、新規症例や具体的な感染状況の報告はなく情報不足のため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 本記事の主題は南スーダン・イバ郡における治安・交通インフラの問題であり、エボラはDRCにおける既知の流行への言及として扱われている。南スーダンは対象国リストに含まれないため除外し、言及されたDRCのみ記載。具体的な症例数や新規発生の情報は記事内になく、既存流行の越境影響に関する報告と判断。

article.articleHeadline: Gangapar News: जसरा में लम्पी बीमारी का गांव-गांव टीकाकरण शुरू
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Gangapar News: Lumpy Skin Disease vaccination starts village-to-village in Jasra
article.articleSummary: As of 5 October 2026, vaccination against Lumpy Skin Disease (LSD) is being rolled out village by village in Jasra block, launched at the Government Ayurvedic Hospital Jasra and the Government Ayurvedic Veterinary Hospital Jasra. LSD is a viral disease affecting cattle (cows and buffaloes) and spreads readily between animals; farmers are not at risk. Vaccination is conducted in two shifts: 09:00–13:00 and 14:00–18:00. Vaccination has already been carried out in villages including Kanjasa, Birwal, Mankawar, Rera, Gadara, Bikar, Sadwa, Tatarganj, Pachkhara, and Chhatara. Owners are advised to seek immediate veterinary consultation and treatment if symptoms appear in their animals. Dr. Chandrasekhar Pal, chief veterinary officer, stated vaccination and treatment are underway to curb the outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: Gangapar News: ジャスラで小結節性皮膚病（ランピースキン病）の村ごとのワクチン接種開始
triage.triage_reason: 動物感染症（ランピースキン病）で人への感染リスクはなく、既に行政によるワクチン接種対応が進められている通常の家畜衛生対応であり、公衆衛生上の懸念は低い。
triage.notes: ランピースキン病は牛・水牛のみに感染するウイルス性疾患で、人獣共通感染症ではない。記事は地方の家畜ワクチン接種活動の通常報道。
