article.articleHeadline: Penularan Influenza A Meningkat, Dinkes Sulsel Minta Warga Tak Panik
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Influenza A Transmission Increasing, South Sulawesi Health Office Urges Residents Not to Panic.
article.articleSummary: Influenza A transmission is increasing nationally in Indonesia, prompting South Sulawesi's Health Office (Dinkes Sulsel) to heighten vigilance. In Makassar, authorities are expanding surveillance for influenza-like illness (ILI) and severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) in line with Ministry of Health directives. Health officials note the uptick occurred August–September 2026 but remains within expected seasonal patterns observed in Indonesia and other ASEAN countries. Subtypes circulating include H1N1 and H3N2; infections can range from mild to severe. Health facilities from community clinics (puskesmas) to hospitals are being kept ready for detection, testing, monitoring, and management based on clinical severity. For mild cases, rest and supportive care; for severe or high-risk patients, more advanced medical treatment is provided. Officials stress: public should stay vigilant but not panic.

triage.headline_ja: インフルエンザA型の感染が増加、南スラウェシ州保健局が住民にパニックにならないよう呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザ（H1N1/H3N2）の増加であり、当局は季節的パターンの範囲内としているが、サーベイランス強化の動きがあるため継続監視とする。
triage.notes: 当局は季節的範囲内の増加と説明しており、重症度や異常性に関する情報は限定的。続報で重症例・死亡者数等の推移を確認する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Pneumonic Plague Death In Russia Triggers Global Scare: How Deadly Is This Disease Symptoms And Treatment Explained
article.articleSummary: Death of a 28-year-old laboratory technician in Russia's Irkutsk region, Siberia, from suspected pneumonic plague triggers global concern over a possible outbreak. Plague is caused by Yersinia pestis and transmitted to humans via flea bites, contact with infected animals or tissues, or inhalation of infectious respiratory droplets. The WHO recognizes three forms: bubonic, pneumonic, and septicaemic; pneumonic plague, which affects the lungs, is the most dangerous and contagious, capable of spreading between people through respiratory particles and can progress rapidly. Incubation is typically 1–7 days, though pneumonic plague can develop faster. Treatment hinges on early antibiotic therapy. Prevention emphasizes avoiding contact with infected animals, fleas, tissues, and body fluids, and following health authorities’ guidance when plague is present. Notably, most recent human cases have occurred in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Madagascar, underscoring global vigilance.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアでの肺ペスト死亡例が世界的懸念を引き起こす:この致死性疾患の症状と治療法を解説
triage.triage_reason: ロシア・イルクーツクで研究室技術者1名が肺ペストで死亡した単発事例であり、対象国への直接的な影響は確認されていない。ヒト-ヒト感染の可能性がある重篤な疾患だが、現時点で拡大や渡航制限等の情報は不足しており、続報の注視が妥当。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はロシア（イルクーツク州）での単発の肺ペスト死亡例。DRC・マダガスカルは『近年の人的症例が多い地域』という背景説明として言及されているのみで、本件の発生地域ではないため対象国リストからは除外。ロシアは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations は空配列。

article.articleHeadline: Influenza A di Indonesia dan Apa yang Perlu Kita Tahu?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Influenza A in Indonesia and What Do We Need to Know?
article.articleSummary: Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 dominates influenza findings in Indonesia in September 2026, with laboratory data showing H1N1pdm09 as the prevailing subtype (week 38 of 2026). In Tangerang Regency, Banten, influenza A cases rose to about 5,000 per month during August–September 2026, attributed to extreme weather and dust pollution from a prolonged dry season. Compared with seasonal flu, Influenza A features abrupt onset with high fever (38–40°C), severe body aches, headaches, sore throat, cough, and extreme fatigue, sometimes with nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea; it can lead to pneumonia or respiratory failure, especially in vulnerable groups. Transmission is via droplets and contaminated surfaces; continual antigenic drift and shift drive evolution, necessitating yearly vaccine updates. High-risk groups include the elderly (65+), children under 5, pregnant women, and people with chronic illnesses or obesity. Prevention centers on vaccination, with government response noted but the article ends mid-sentence.

triage.headline_ja: インドネシアにおけるインフルエンザA、私たちが知っておくべきこと
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザA(H1N1)pdm09による国内患者数増加であり、異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められず、既知の季節性流行の範疇にとどまる。
triage.notes: H1N1pdm09は既に季節性株として定着しており、乾季の気象要因・大気汚染による患者増と説明されている。パンデミック性の新規性は認められない。

article.articleHeadline: RDC eleva a cerca de 8.500 los casos de ébola, con alrededor de...
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC raises the number of Ebola cases to about 8,500, with around ....
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (Ituri epicenter) has reached about 8,500 confirmed cases and around 4,100 deaths as of Oct 5, 2026. The INSP reported 8,442 infections and 4,080 deaths, including 66 cases and 38 deaths in the last 24 hours after a new health zone was affected in North Kivu. There are 846 hospitalized or isolated patients and 2,213 recoveries; the case fatality rate is 48.3%, with contact tracing at 73.1%. Ituri still accounts for roughly 75% of cases, affecting seven provinces: Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Upper Uele, Lower Uele, Tshopo, and Ubangi-Sud. Active community transmission is noted in Ituri, North Kivu and Upper Uele; Ubangi-Sud had no cases in the last 24 hours, and Tshopo none in the last 72 hours. This is the deadliest Ebola outbreak in DRC history, with projections that it could surpass the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: DRCのエボラ感染者数が約8,500人に増加、死者は約4,100人に
triage.triage_reason: 致死率48.3%の大規模エボラ流行がDRC史上最悪となり、複数州にまたがり地域社会感染が継続しているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: DRC史上最大のエボラ流行であり、2014-2016年西アフリカ流行を上回る可能性が指摘されている。7州に拡大し、イツリ・北キブ・オートウエレで地域社会感染が継続中。既にフルRRA相当の重大イベントと判断。

article.articleHeadline: دويتشه فيله : فيروس حمى قرية "سيندبيس" المصرية يصيب أول إنسان في ألمانيا ! - عكس السير
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Deutsche Welle: The Sindbis fever virus from the Egyptian village Sindbis infects the first person in Germany!
article.articleSummary: Germany reports the first laboratory-confirmed Sindbis fever case in Baden-Württemberg. A 60-year-old man from Stuttgart was infected on 12 July; the infection was confirmed in September 2026 by the Robert Koch Institute, and he is recovering without symptoms. The case indicates local Sindbis virus circulation in Germany, with previous undetected infections found among Weinheim blood donors. Sindbis virus primarily infects birds and is transmitted by mosquitoes; it does not spread human-to-human. It is found across Eurasia and Africa; disease is usually mild or asymptomatic, but can cause fever, itchy rash, and joint pain, with arthritis lasting months in some cases. No specific antiviral treatment exists; care is supporting. Clinicians should consider Sindbis during mosquito season for febrile patients with rash and arthralgia, even without travel. Isolation was in 1952 in Egypt's Nile Delta, named after Sindbis village; human cases occurred in Uganda (1961), South Africa (1963), Australia (1967).

triage.headline_ja: ドイチェ・ヴェレ:エジプトの村「シンドビス」由来のシンドビス熱ウイルス、ドイツで初のヒト感染例
triage.triage_reason: ドイツでの単発の軽症例であり、ヒト-ヒト感染もなく、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクも低いため見送りと判断。
triage.notes: 発生地域にタイ(Bangkok)が含まれるが記事本文では言及されておらず、実際の感染地はドイツ(Baden-Württemberg)及び歴史的言及のエジプト・ウガンダ・南アフリカ・オーストラリア。いずれも対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsは空。単発軽症例でヒト-ヒト感染なし、蚊媒介性のため拡大リスク低い。

article.articleHeadline: Pneumonic plague case in Russia raises questions: How it spreads and what Indians should know
article.articleSummary: Pneumonic plague case reported in Irkutsk, Siberia, Russia, with hundreds quarantined after a 28-year-old laboratory technician reportedly died; authorities say the death was from an unspecified form of plague, though pneumonic plague is under discussion. Pneumonic plague is caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis and spreads mainly via close contact through respiratory droplets. Symptoms include high fever, chills, weakness, cough, chest pain and breathing difficulty; bloody or watery sputum may occur. Unlike Covid-19, plague is bacterial and antibiotics are effective when given promptly; early clinical assessment and laboratory confirmation are essential. Public-health guidance advises India not to panic—plague remains rare there, but awareness is important: avoid exposure to rodents and sick animals, minimize close contact with suspected cases, and seek medical attention for sudden fever with rapidly worsening respiratory symptoms; do not self-medicate with antibiotics.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアでの肺ペスト症例が疑問を呼ぶ：どのように広がるか、インド人が知っておくべきこと
triage.triage_reason: ロシア（イルクーツク）での単発の肺ペスト疑い死亡例であり、対象国での発生ではないが、ヒト-ヒト感染の可能性がある病原体のため続報を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はロシア・イルクーツクでの肺ペスト（疑い）症例であり、インドは対象国リストに含まれるが、記事内ではインド読者向けの注意喚起情報として言及されているのみで、インド国内での実際の発生ではないため verified_locations には含めない。ロシアは対象国リストに含まれないため、該当国はなし。

article.articleHeadline: Kolom Pakar: 5 Hal tentang Penyakit Pes di Rusia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Expert Column: 5 Things About the Plague in Russia.
article.articleSummary: Nearly 200 people are under observation in Russia after an Irkutsk laboratory worker died from plague, per a Moscow Times report on 2 October 2026. The piece outlines five key points about plague (Yersinia pestis): it is a zoonotic bacterium transmitted from animals to humans and potentially between people via contact with infected materials or inhalation. There are three main forms: Bubonic plague, septicemic plague, and pneumonic plague; Russia reports include pneumonia, though exact manifestations are still under investigation. Bubonic plague has a case fatality rate of 30–60%, while pneumonic plague is highly lethal if treatment is delayed. Historical context cites the Black Death (1346–1353) and early-20th-century outbreaks in Java (per BRIN). BRIN notes Indonesia is not fully plague-free due to a silent period with enzootic reservoirs like fleas and rats. Monitor Russia closely and maintain vigilance for Indonesia."

triage.headline_ja: 専門家コラム：ロシアのペストに関する5つのポイント
triage.triage_reason: ロシア（イルクーツク）の検査室職員の死亡例を中心とした記事で、対象国（インドネシア等）での実際の患者発生は確認されていない。ペストの重篤性・人-人感染の可能性から国際的な警戒は必要だが、対象国への直接的関連は現時点で不明なため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 記事はインドネシアのメディアによるロシアでのペスト流行に関する解説コラムで、インドネシアにおける警戒喚起（過去のジャワでの流行歴・ペスト未根絶の可能性）が述べられているが、現在インドネシアで患者が発生しているわけではないため、verified_locationsには含めない。ロシア（対象国外）での動向を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Warga Tertular Antraks di Gunungkidul, Dosen UGM Jangan Konsumsi Daging Hewan Sakit
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Residents Infected with Anthrax in Gunungkidul, UGM Lecturer: Do Not Consume Meat from Sick Animals
article.articleSummary: Anthrax resurfaces in Gunungkidul, Yogyakarta Special Region (DIY), Indonesia, with four residents in Dusun Pelem, Semanu testing positive for Bacillus anthracis. Nanung Danar Dono, a lecturer at Gadjah Mada University’s Faculty of Animal Science (Fapet UGM) and Halal Centre member, notes anthrax as a zoonosis requiring strict handling of affected animals, since Gunungkidul is an endemic area. Do not slaughter or consume meat from sick or suddenly dead livestock; report carcasses to authorities because Bacillus anthracis spores can persist and spread. Human infection can occur via ingestion, inhalation, or skin contact; animals may exhibit sudden death with high fever and loss of appetite. Epidemiology: seven suspected cases; four PCR-confirmed positives; 47 people at risk exposed to animals or products from four goats that died suddenly (brandu). The four positives have recovered after treatment; exposed individuals received antibiotic prophylaxis and are monitored for 60 days (two incubation periods).

triage.headline_ja: グンキドゥルで住民が炭疽菌に感染、UGM講師「病気の動物の肉を食べないで」
triage.triage_reason: グンキドゥル（ジョグジャカルタ）は炭疽菌の流行地域であり、今回も家畜由来の感染が確認されたが、患者は回復済みで重症例・死亡例はなく、ヒト-ヒト感染リスクもないため、既知の局地的なアウトブレイクとして経過観察が妥当。
triage.notes: グンキドゥルは炭疽菌の既知の流行地域。感染経路は病死した家畜（ヤギ）の解体・摂取によるもので、人獣共通感染症としての管理は地元レベルで対応可能。47名の曝露者には抗生物質予防投与と60日間の経過観察が実施されており、公衆衛生対応は適切に機能している。

article.articleHeadline: La France réaffirme son soutien à la lutte contre Ebola en République démocratique du Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: France reaffirms its support for the fight against Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: France reaffirms support for Ebola response in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot announcing intensified backing for researchers, health and humanitarian personnel to eradicate the outbreak. He visited Bunia in eastern DRC, described as the outbreak’s epicenter, where about 8,000 confirmed cases and 4,000 deaths—roughly a quarter among children—have been recorded. Bunia hosts the outbreak response command center since May, and containment efforts have so far prevented spread to major urban centers in Africa, French overseas territories, or Europe. France commits to mobilizing from day one to assist researchers and frontline responders, highlighting that Ebola and other viruses cross borders and must be tackled at the source. Barrot also lauded French researchers and humanitarian workers leading the response on the ground.

triage.headline_ja: フランス、コンゴ民主共和国におけるエボラ対策への支援を改めて表明
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で約8,000症例・4,000死亡という大規模なエボラ流行が継続しており、IHR基準の複数（深刻性・異常性・国際拡大リスク）に該当するためフルリスク評価が妥当。
triage.notes: フランス外相がブニア（流行の震源地）を訪問し支援強化を表明した記事。流行自体はDRC国内に限局しており、主要都市やフランス海外領土、欧州への拡大は現時点で防がれていると記載されているが、エボラの性質上国際拡大リスクは依然として懸念される。フランスは支援提供国であり発生国ではないためverified_locationsには含めない。

article.articleHeadline: DRC - Concept of Operations - Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) Outbreak, October 2026
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo virus disease (EVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) declared 15 May 2026 after laboratory confirmation of the Bundibugyo strain in Ituri Province. As of 26 September 2026, the outbreak remains concentrated in eastern DRC with 8,067 confirmed cases and 3,901 deaths across 63 health zones in seven provinces: Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uélé, Bas-Uélé, Tshopo, and Sud-Ubangi. Uganda declared the end of the outbreak in late August 2026 after a 42‑day surveillance with no onward transmission. WHO declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on 17 May 2026. No vaccine is available for the Bundibugyo strain. The outbreak risks regional spread to Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, Central African Republic, and South Sudan, with potential spread to urban centers Butembo and Kisangani. Ongoing insecurity, displacement, difficult terrain, and limited health access hinder response; this marks the DRC’s seventeenth Ebola outbreak. The Ministry of Health has called for mobilization of technical and financial partners.

triage.headline_ja: DRC - エボラウイルス病（EVD）流行に関するオペレーション概要、2026年10月
triage.triage_reason: WHOがPHEICを宣言したブンディブギョ株によるエボラ流行で、8,000例超・死亡3,901例、ワクチン未承認かつ周辺国への拡大リスクがあり、IHR基準・WPRO基準の双方で複数該当するため。
triage.notes: ウガンダは既に流行終息が宣言されており、対象国リストに該当する国はDRCのみ。ルワンダ、ブルンジ、中央アフリカ、南スーダンは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Quyết tâm phòng, chống bệnh dại
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Determination to Prevent and Control Rabies
article.articleSummary: Six rabies deaths were recorded in Ho Chi Minh City in 2026 through mid-September, with four animal outbreaks detected in Long Son Commune, Tru Van Tho Commune, Phuoc Thang Ward, and Tan Hai Ward. Health facilities have treated more than 100,000 bite-and-scratch injuries from dogs and cats, a rise of about 11% versus the previous year. The city’s animal health department reports 24 communes/wards have begun capturing roaming dogs; nearly 500 dogs have been seized, including over 170 in Con Dao Special Administrative Region and more than 70 in Dong Hoa Ward. Fines of 1–2 million VND apply for not muzzling or leashing dogs or for not having a handler in public. Long Hai Commune registered 3 rabies deaths and 169 suspected bite reports, prompting intensified prevention measures, especially targeting children, and vaccination to achieve 80% herd immunity. Officials aim for zero human rabies deaths by 2030; a World Rabies Day event in Long Hai emphasized collective action with the theme “Stronger Together.”

triage.headline_ja: 狂犬病の予防・対策への決意
triage.triage_reason: ホーチミン市で狂犬病による死亡6名と複数の動物感染事例が報告されており、咬傷件数も増加傾向にあるため、重症度・持続的曝露・流行可能性の観点でスクリーニング基準に該当し、行政・地域の関心も高いことからフルリスク評価への移行を検討すべき。
triage.notes: 狂犬病はベトナムで地域的に流行している疾患であり、本記事は既存の対策キャンペーン（犬の捕獲、ワクチン接種、罰金制度など）の進捗報告が中心。ただし死亡者数・咬傷件数の増加が見られるため、継続的なモニタリングが望ましい。

article.articleHeadline: La Jornada: Rusia descarta brote epidemiológico en Irkutsk
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: La Jornada: Russia rules out an epidemiological outbreak in Irkutsk.
article.articleSummary: Quarantine for three weeks and isolation of at least four major hospitals in Irkutsk, near Lake Baikal, to contain rumors of an outbreak. Since Oct 2, after the death of a patient with suspected pneumonic plague bacteria, speculation of an epidemic in Irkutsk and nearby Shelekhov (about 20 km away) spread online. Daria Shipilova, 28, a researcher at the Institute of Plague Research in Siberia and the Far East, was admitted to a hospital in Shelekhov on Sept 29 and died two days later. Governor Igor Kobtsev and health official Anna Popova stated the epidemiological situation is stable. The federal surveillance service described the case as pneumonia of unknown etiology and noted special measures related to an employee of the plague institute. No confirmed pneumonic plague outbreak; claims of Thailand exposure or a lab spill were speculative.

triage.headline_ja: ラ・ホルナダ紙：ロシア、イルクーツクでの疫学的アウトブレイクを否定
triage.triage_reason: ペスト研究所の研究者が肺ペスト疑いで死亡し、イルクーツクで複数病院の隔離・3週間の検疫措置が取られるなど、公式否定にもかかわらず重大な公衆衛生対応が発生しているため、フルリスク評価への移行が妥当。
triage.notes: 事象の発生地はロシア・イルクーツク州であり、対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsは空。タイへの曝露疑惑は記事中で『憶測』と明記されており、実際の発生国とは認められない。公式には肺ペストのアウトブレイクを否定し『原因不明の肺炎』としているが、ペスト研究所職員の死亡という異例性から続報の注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: 200 personnes à l'isolement, des hôpitaux bouclés : après le décès suspect d'une jeune technicienne de laboratoire en Sibérie, la peste sévit-elle en Russie ?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 200 people in isolation, hospitals locked down: after the suspected death of a young laboratory technician in Siberia, is the plague sweeping through Russia?
article.articleSummary: Suspected pneumonic plague emerges in Siberia following the death of a 28-year-old laboratory technician at Irkutsk’s plague research institute in Chelekhov. The patient, Daria Shipilova, was admitted Sept 29, 2026, and died Oct 2 after an acute pulmonary illness. Russian authorities’ Rospotrebnadzor classify the illness as pneumonia of undetermined etiology and say no pathogen linked to the institute’s activities has been detected, while local clinicians and a regional leader publicly warn of pneumonic plague. Two unconfirmed scenarios include private travel to Thailand or an accidental tube breakage at the institute. A three-week isolation protocol covers several Irkutsk facilities, and about 200 people who had contact with the patient are under preventive medical surveillance. On Oct 3, the Chelekhov aluminum plant made masks mandatory; Baikalsk briefly advised avoiding Chelekhov. U.S. officials say Washington is monitoring; Russian authorities report no additional symptomatic cases among those isolated and the situation remains under control.

triage.headline_ja: 200人が隔離、病院封鎖：シベリアの若手研究技師の疑わしい死亡後、ロシアでペストが流行しているのか？
triage.triage_reason: ペスト研究所関連で研究技師が急性肺疾患により死亡し、肺ペストの疑いがあるとして200人が隔離・複数施設が封鎖されるなど、重大性・異常性・流行可能性が高く、国際的な監視（米国当局が注視）も確認されるためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 発生国はロシア（対象国リスト外）のため verified_locations は空。タイへの渡航歴は未確認の仮説の一つであり、タイでの発生事実はないため含めない。病原体はRospotrebnadzorにより未確定（原因不明肺炎として扱われている）。

article.articleHeadline: Ruang Rawat Rumah Sakit di Cimahi Penuh, Dinkes Buka Suara Soal Isu Influenza A
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Hospital Wards in Cimahi Are Full, Health Department Speaks Out on Influenza A Issue
article.articleSummary: Full inpatient wards in Cimahi, Indonesia, with RSUD Cibabat reporting longer waits in the emergency department due to bed shortages. Dinas Kesehatan Kota Cimahi (Dinkes) clarifies that these occupancy issues are not linked to Influenza A, stating that no confirmed Influenza A cases have been reported to the city health office based on SKDR data. Nonetheless, officials note a rise in Acute Respiratory Infections (ISPA/ARI) in Cimahi. September 2026 surveillance recorded 2,675 ARI cases, and week 38 saw a notable surge. Mulyati, head of Dinkes Kota Cimahi, urged the public not to panic and advised anyone with symptoms to visit a Puskesmas for an accurate examination; depending on assessment, patients may be treated at home or referred for further care.

triage.headline_ja: チマヒ市の病院病棟が満床、保健局がインフルエンザA型の噂について見解を表明
triage.triage_reason: インフルエンザA型の確定例は報告されておらず当局が否定しているが、ARI症例の増加が報告されており続報を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: インフルエンザA型の確定例は否定されており、病床逼迫はARI(急性呼吸器感染症)の増加によるものとされる。当局は市民にパニックを避けるよう呼びかけている。

article.articleHeadline: Delapan wilayah di Manokwari KLB campak-rubella, Pemkab gencar gelar imunisasi
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Eight areas in Manokwari hit by a measles-rubella outbreak; the regency government intensifies immunization campaigns.
article.articleSummary: Measles-Rubella outbreak declared in eight areas of Manokwari Regency, West Papua, Indonesia, with 70 suspected cases. Health authorities declared a Public Health Emergency (KLB) and are intensifying vaccination campaigns targeting children aged nine months to five years. Vaccinations were administered at PAUD Terpadu Negeri Pembina Manokwari on Monday, 5 October 2026, as health workers push MR immunization to contain transmission. The response is led by the Manokwari Regency Health Office across eight affected localities; laboratory confirmation is not stated, with cases currently classified as suspected. The report emphasizes ongoing outbreak management and public health measures to safeguard young children in the region.

triage.headline_ja: マノクワリの8地域で麻疹・風疹アウトブレイク、県政府がワクチン接種を強化
triage.triage_reason: 麻疹・風疹の地域的アウトブレイク（疑い症例70例、公衆衛生緊急事態宣言）だが、検査確定情報がなく国際的拡大リスクも限定的なため、続報を注視する段階と判断。
triage.notes: 検査確定症例数、重症度（入院・死亡）、他地域への拡大状況が記事に記載されておらず不明。地方政府主導で対応中であり外部支援の必要性は不明。

article.articleHeadline: 本港一周錄得兩宗退伍軍人病個案｜METROHK.com.hk
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Two cases of veterans' illness recorded in Hong Kong in one week
article.articleSummary: Two cases of Legionnaires' disease were recorded in Hong Kong from Sep 27 to Oct 3, 2026, comprising a 67-year-old man in the Southern District with community-acquired infection and a 55-year-old woman who had traveled to Mainland China during the incubation period, classified as imported. As of Oct 3, 2026, Hong Kong's total is 153 cases this year. Authorities say these are sporadic with no epidemiological link to earlier HK cases. Historical totals: 2025, 167 cases; 2024, 135. Risk factors include male sex, age over 50, smoking, alcohol use, and immunocompromise. Environmental sources include poorly maintained water systems, hot-water systems, cooling towers, spas, fountains, humidifiers, and home medical equipment. Transmission is via inhalation of aerosolized contaminated water. The Department of Health is conducting epidemiological investigations and issuing guidance on water safety, humidifier use, and alternatives to filtration; smoking cessation and alcohol screening resources are offered.

triage.headline_ja: 香港で1週間に退役軍人病（レジオネラ症）2例を記録
triage.triage_reason: 散発例であり既往症例との疫学的関連もなく、季節的な通常範囲内の発生数であるため特段のシグナルとはみなされない。
triage.notes: レジオネラ症は人-人感染せず、過去数年と同程度の発生数で推移しており、当局も散発例と評価している。

article.articleHeadline: India's top killer diseases have changed, but TB and infections still won't go away
article.articleSummary: WHO Global Health Estimates (2000–2023) show India’s biggest killer in 2023 is ischaemic heart disease at 138.5 deaths per 100,000, followed by stroke (74.8), COPD (83.19) and diabetes (49.01). The shift from 2000 is stark: TB (92.4) and diarrhoeal diseases (87.8) led mortality then. Infections persist: TB, diarrhoeal diseases and lower respiratory infections remain among the top 10 causes, alongside cardiovascular and metabolic diseases. Diarrhoeal deaths declined markedly—from about 1.46 million in 1990 to 462,220 in 2023, with a crude death rate of 32/100,000—thanks to sanitation, safe water, vaccination and treatment access. TB remains a major challenge globally and in India. A GBD 2023 analysis notes COPD, ischaemic heart disease and stroke as large contributors to tobacco-attributable deaths in India. By 2023, non-communicable diseases account for ~75% of top-10 deaths ( communicable ~16%), while road injuries rank 10th with ~174,000 deaths (about 14% of roughly 12.2 lakh global road deaths).

triage.headline_ja: インドの主要死因は変化したが、結核と感染症は依然として残っている
triage.triage_reason: WHOの統計データに基づく疾病負荷の経年変化を扱う一般的な保健統計記事であり、急性の公衆衛生危機や異常事態を示すものではない。
triage.notes: 記事はインドの慢性疾患・感染症による死亡率の長期トレンド分析であり、結核は依然として上位死因の一つとして言及されているが、新規アウトブレイクや急性事象ではないため、対象国リストに含まれるインドであっても疫学的シグナルとはみなさない。

article.articleHeadline: ಡೆಂಗ್ಯೂ ಭೀತಿ: ನಿಮ್ಮ ಬಾಲ್ಕನಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸೊಳ್ಳೆಗಳ ಸಂತಾನೋತ್ಪತ್ತಿ ತಡೆಯಲು 10 ನಿಮಿಷದ ಸಿಂಪಲ್ ಟಿಪ್ಸ್!
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue fear: 10-minute simple tips to prevent mosquitoes from breeding on your balcony!
article.articleSummary: Dengue outbreaks intensify in India: Lucknow reports 87 dengue cases in days after heavy rains; Chennai records 1,290 infections in September; Tamil Nadu sees about 200 daily cases this week. Aedes mosquitoes bite during the day; their eggs hatch within 48 hours in warm weather. A 10-minute balcony check can curb breeding by eliminating standing water in pots, trays, buckets, pet bowls, and fridge drip trays; raise containers and ensure proper drainage. Install sturdy window and balcony screens (min 18x16 cm; 20x20 cm in high-risk areas) and seal edges with brush or magnetic strips. Conduct 48-hour water reminders for plants, coolers, and bird-water containers; if water cannot be emptied, apply approved larvicides. For 1,000 L of water, add 2 mL temephos 50% EC (1 mg/L); BTI may be used for drinking water. Keep water sources closed, pump out basement stagnation, and maintain 0.2–0.5 mg/L chlorine in drinking water. Do not use lemon eucalyptus oil for children under 3; seek medical care for high fever, bleeding, or persistent vomiting.

triage.headline_ja: デング熱への不安：バルコニーでの蚊の繁殖を防ぐ10分間の簡単なヒント！
triage.triage_reason: インド各地（ラクナウ、チェンナイ、タミル・ナードゥ州）でデング熱症例が増加しているが、季節性の雨季に伴う例年通りの流行であり異常性は低く、記事自体も予防啓発が主目的のため、フルRRAに進めるほどの緊急性は確認できない。
triage.notes: 記事は主に蚊の繁殖防止に関する家庭向け予防ガイドであり、ラクナウ（87例）、チェンナイ（9月に1290例）、タミル・ナードゥ州（週200例程度）のデング熱症例数が言及されているが、季節性の雨季に伴う例年の流行パターンの範囲内とみられる。重症度や国際的拡大の情報はなし。

article.articleHeadline: Bird Flu in Anantapur: 2,500 Chickens Die
article.articleSummary: As of 5 October 2026, avian influenza has been confirmed in Siddarampuram village, Bukkarayasamudram taluk, Anantapur district, Andhra Pradesh, after about 2,500 native chickens died over the past month. Lab tests on dead birds confirmed infection at the High Security Animal Disease Laboratory in Bhopal. The district administration and animal husbandry department intensified surveillance and containment, including spraying sodium hypochlorite, monitoring surrounding areas, and strengthening isolation. Veterinary teams advise poultry owners to report unusual deaths and follow preventive guidance. Health authorities urge residents to seek medical care for fever or respiratory symptoms. The outbreak has caused roughly ₹10 lakh in losses for poultry farmers, underscoring livelihood impacts, with ongoing field monitoring and preventive actions to limit further spread.

triage.headline_ja: アナンタプルで鳥インフルエンザ発生：鶏2,500羽が死亡
triage.triage_reason: アーンドラ・プラデーシュ州の家禽における鳥インフルエンザ確認事例であり、人への感染は報告されていないが、亜型不明かつ継続的な監視対象であるため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 本事例は家禽（在来鶏）の大量死に関するものであり、人への感染は確認されていない。ウイルス亜型（H5N1等）の記載なし。当局による消毒・監視強化等の防疫対応は実施中。人獣共通感染症としての継続監視が望ましい。

article.articleHeadline: Vědkyně na Sibiři zemřela na zápal plic neznámého původu. Lékaři monitorují stovky lidí
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A female scientist in Siberia died of pneumonia of unknown origin. Doctors are monitoring hundreds of people.
article.articleSummary: In Russia’s Siberian Irkutsk region, a 28-year-old female scientist at an anti-plague institute died; authorities have not officially confirmed the cause, though NBC News cited pneumonia of unknown origin. Local officials closed the hospital ward where she was treated and placed nearly 200 people in preventive medical observation who had direct or indirect contact. Pneumonic plague, caused by Yersinia pestis, can spread between people via airborne droplets and can trigger serious epidemics unless rapidly treated with potent antibiotics. The United States is monitoring the situation with the CDC and has urged Russian authorities to share information promptly; WHO and the Kremlin did not immediately comment. Ashish Jha called for greater transparency and noted concerns about potential bioweapons programs in the region. Global data (2019–2025) show over 3,800 suspected plague cases in 10 countries, mainly in the DRC and Madagascar.

triage.headline_ja: シベリアの女性科学者が原因不明の肺炎で死亡。医師らは数百人を監視下に置く
triage.triage_reason: 抗ペスト研究所関係者が原因不明の肺炎（肺ペストの疑い）で死亡し、約200人が予防的観察下に置かれ、米国CDCも監視するなど国際的関心が高いため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 発生地域はロシア（イルクーツク州）であり、対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsは空とした。DRC・Madagascarは過去の世界的ペスト症例データの文脈で言及されているのみで、本イベントの発生地ではない。公式な原因確定（肺ペストか否か）は未発表であり、続報を要する。

article.articleHeadline: कितना खतरनाक है प्लेग? रूस की लैब से निकली बीमारी, ले चुकी है 8 करोड़ जानें
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: How dangerous is the plague? A disease that emerged from a lab in Russia has claimed 80 million lives.
article.articleSummary: As of 5 October 2026, in Siberia at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute near Shelekhov, a 28-year-old scientist, Darya Shipilova, died on 2 October 2026 after a test tube containing live Yersinia pestis (plague) broke during lab work. About 197 colleagues and staff have been quarantined, and five major hospitals are on high alert; no infections have been detected among exposed individuals, and initial tests are negative with masks enforced around the facility. Pneumonic plague, the likely form, can spread via respiratory droplets and can cause fatal lung damage within 24–48 hours if untreated. Historically, plague has caused tens of millions of deaths across Europe, Asia, and India. Russian authorities have convened an emergency meeting and continue medical surveillance of those exposed.

triage.headline_ja: プレーグとはどれほど危険か？ロシアの研究所から流出した病原体、過去に8000万人の命を奪った疾病
triage.triage_reason: ロシアの研究所で致死性ペスト菌（肺ペスト疑い）による研究者死亡事故が発生し、異常事態かつ重篤な公衆衛生上の懸念があるため、IHR基準を2つ満たしフルRRAへの移行が妥当。
triage.notes: 事故はロシア・シベリアの研究所内で発生し、対象国リストに含まれるインドは歴史的言及のみでイベント発生国ではないため verified_locations は空とした。現時点で二次感染は確認されておらず、隔離対応が継続中。

article.articleHeadline: No immediate risk to India, says Kerala medical body expert amid pneumonic plague scare in Russia
article.articleSummary: Unverified reports of a suspected fatal pneumonic plague case in Russia prompted Kerala State Indian Medical Association's Rajeev Jayadevan to stress contact tracing and say there is no immediate risk to India. Yersinia pestis causes plague with three forms: skin, pneumonia, and septicemia; pneumonic plague attacks the lungs and can kill within 24 hours. A lab worker reportedly died of pneumonia, with a test tube containing Y. pestis in the lab; diagnosis not confirmed upfront. Contacts are being traced and monitored, with preventive antibiotics offered to those at risk. There is no travel-related risk to India; transmission is more likely in crowded settings when patients are severely ill. Pneumonic plague symptoms include fever, cranial discomfort, and fatigue, preceding rapid pneumonia, breathing difficulties, chest discomfort, coughing, and sometimes blood-tinged or fluid secretions.

triage.headline_ja: ケララ州医師会の専門家、ロシアでの肺ペスト懸念の中でインドへの直接的リスクはないと発言
triage.triage_reason: ロシアでの未確認の単発肺ペスト疑い例に関する報道であり、対象国での発生ではなく、インドへの言及も「リスクなし」とのコメントに留まるため、続報を注視する。
triage.notes: 事例発生地はロシアであり対象国リストに含まれない。インドは専門家コメントの文脈でのみ言及され、実際の発生国ではないためverified_locationsは空とした。診断も未確定（unverified）の段階。

article.articleHeadline: Smrt v ruské laboratoři: Vrátí se obávaný plicní mor?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Death in a Russian laboratory: Will the dreaded pneumonic plague return?
article.articleSummary: Incident in Shchelkovo near Irkutsk, Siberia, after a laboratory worker at the anti-plague institute died from severe pneumonia, prompted warnings of pneumonic plague. Roughly 200 potentially exposed people were placed under medical surveillance; authorities say the death was pneumonia of unknown origin, with no plague organisms detected in tested samples, and the epidemiological situation is stable. Pneumonic plague—caused by Yersinia pestis—is the most severe yet rare form and can arise from inhalation or progression from other forms. It spreads between people via respiratory droplets; close, prolonged contact is typical. Incubation is 1–3 days; symptoms include high fever, headache, cough, dyspnea, chest pain, rapid pneumonia, and hemoptysis. Early antibiotics (gentamicin, doxycycline, fluoroquinolones) greatly improve survival. Isolation and droplet precautions are recommended; no special negative-pressure ventilation required. Endemic foci exist in DRC, Madagascar, Peru; occasional cases in the US; historical links to the Soviet bio program.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアの研究所での死亡事故：恐れられている肺ペストは再来するのか？
triage.triage_reason: シベリアの抗ペスト研究所職員が重症肺炎で死亡し肺ペストの疑いが報じられたが、検体からペスト菌は検出されず当局は状況安定と発表しており、現時点では確証情報が不足しているため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 事件はロシア（シベリア・イルクーツク州）で発生しており、対象国リストに該当する国はない。記事中でDRC、マダガスカル、ペルーは風土病流行地としての背景情報のみで、今回の事例発生地ではないため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola : autour de la RDC, surveiller aussi les passages informels et les voies fluviales
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: around the DRC, also monitor informal crossings and river routes.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo prompts neighboring countries to bolster preparedness by monitoring informal crossings and river routes. An International Organization for Migration report (Sept 14–20) outlines mapping movements and targeting alert points to guide interventions. In the Central African Republic, north of the DRC, 42 authorities and community representatives mapped routes in Mbomou to identify priority paths for surveillance. In Uganda, 12 observation points monitor population movements, with seven along the Congolese border, augmenting sanitary travel checks. Cross-border coordination includes three Uganda–DRC meetings that yielded action plans on information sharing and surveillance. River channels are addressed too: in Kisangani, the Congo River without Ebola initiative evaluated ports and control points. These preparations aim to limit spread and do not signify confirmed cases in neighboring countries.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：DRC周辺地域、非公式な越境地点や河川ルートの監視も強化へ
triage.triage_reason: DRC東部でのエボラ流行を受け、周辺国（中央アフリカ共和国、ウガンダ）が国境監視を強化していることが報じられており、国際的拡大リスクへの懸念から継続的な注視が必要。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCでのエボラ流行に対する周辺国（中央アフリカ共和国、ウガンダ）の国境監視強化を主題としており、これらの国で確認症例があるわけではない。対象国リストの中ではDRCのみが実際の感染発生国であるため、verified_locationsにはDRCのみを含めた。中央アフリカ共和国・ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Russian pneumonic plague scare: What it means for India
article.articleSummary: Death of a 28-year-old laboratory worker in Irkutsk raised concerns of pneumonic plague; illness labeled pneumonia of unknown etiology with tests not identifying pathogens linked to her work, and potentially exposed individuals placed under medical observation. Pneumonic plague, caused by Yersinia pestis, infects the lungs and spreads via respiratory droplets; incubation about 1–3 days (range 1–7). Symptoms: sudden high fever, chills, severe headache, weakness, then shortness of breath, chest pain, and a cough with watery, blood-tinged sputum. Antibiotics (e.g., gentamicin, ciprofloxacin, doxycycline) are highly effective if started within 24 hours; delays markedly raise death risk. Post-suspect cases involve isolation in negative-pressure rooms, N95 protection, contact tracing, 7 days of preventive antibiotics, and rapid lab confirmation. For India, risk is virtually zero; Port Health screening at airports, isolation pathways for severely ill travelers, NCDC testing, and ready antibiotic stocks in major hospitals. Emphasis on epidemiological history to distinguish plague from common respiratory illnesses.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアの肺ペスト懸念：インドへの意味
triage.triage_reason: ロシア・イルクーツクで研究所作業員が原因不明の肺炎で死亡し肺ペストが疑われているが、病原体は未確定で単一症例に留まる。対象国での発生ではなく、記事もインドへのリスクはほぼゼロと明記しているため、続報を注視する段階。
triage.notes: 発生国であるロシアは対象国リストに含まれない。記事はインド向けリスク評価記事であり、インド国内での発生事例ではないためverified_locationsは空とした。病原体確認（Yersinia pestis）がまだ未確定である点も要注視。

article.articleHeadline: IMA Expert: No Panic in India Over Russia Plague Case
article.articleSummary: Russia is investigating a suspected fatal case of pneumonic plague after a lab worker’s death; official cause remains unconfirmed. The lab reportedly contained Yersinia pestis, and authorities are tracing contacts. Indian Medical Association (IMA) Research Cell convener Rajeev Jayadevan in New Delhi says there is no need for panic or immediate India threat: plague is well understood, and targeted antibiotics can protect close contacts. Pneumonic plague can spread person-to-person in crowded settings, but most infected individuals are too ill to travel. Authorities emphasize rapid cause identification, exposure history, and contact monitoring. Classic pneumonic-plague symptoms include fever, fatigue, headaches, rapid-onset pneumonia, breathing difficulties, chest pain, coughing, and sometimes blood-tinged or clear fluid secretions; untreated cases can progress to death within about 24 hours. Key measures: contact tracing and laboratory confirmation; current risk to India is negligible.

triage.headline_ja: IMA専門家:ロシアでのペスト症例を受けてもインドでパニックの必要なし
triage.triage_reason: ロシアの研究施設職員の肺ペスト疑い死亡事例で原因未確定、インド専門家は国内への脅威は低いとしているが、確定診断や接触者調査の続報を要する段階。
triage.notes: 事例発生地はロシア(対象国リスト外)。インドは専門家コメントのみで実際の症例なし。原因（Yersinia pestis）の確定や感染拡大状況について続報待ち。

article.articleHeadline: Hampir 4 Ribu Kasus Pes Tercatat dalam 7 Tahun, Ini Peta Sebarannya Menurut WHO
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Almost 4,000 Plague Cases Recorded in 7 Years, Here Is Its Distribution Map According to WHO.
article.articleSummary: Plague (Yersinia pestis) persists globally with nearly 4,000 suspected and confirmed cases reported from 2019–2025 across Africa, Asia, and South America. WHO’s map updated Sept 29 shows ongoing activity in multiple countries; plague circulates in animal reservoirs on all continents except Oceania, with human cases arising when the bacterium jumps from wildlife to people. Most human cases historically come from Africa, notably the Democratic Republic of Congo and Madagascar. Clinical forms include bubonic (most common), pneumonic (airborne, most virulent and capable of human-to-human transmission), and septicemic. Pneumonic plague requires rapid isolation and contact tracing. A Russian incident near Irkutsk involved a lab worker with severe pneumonia; authorities have not confirmed plague as the cause, though about 197 potential contacts were isolated. WHO stresses animal surveillance, rapid case identification, and transmission control to prevent spillover and outbreaks rather than assuming external importation.

triage.headline_ja: 7年間で記録されたペスト症例はほぼ4,000件、WHOによる分布地図
triage.triage_reason: WHOの統計に基づく過去7年間のペスト症例の概観記事であり、新規の急増やアウトブレイクを示す具体的シグナルはないが、DRCなど対象国での継続的な人獣共通感染のリスクがあるため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 記事はWHOの最新マップ（2025年9月29日更新）に基づく過去7年間（2019-2025）のペスト症例の世界的概観であり、DRCとマダガスカルが主要な発生国として挙げられているが、マダガスカルは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。ロシア（イルクーツク）の検査技師の肺炎疑い例は未確認であり対象国でもないため除外。新規の具体的アウトブレイク情報はなく、既存の風土病的状況の統計的整理が中心。

article.articleHeadline: El Kremlin llama a la calma tras alerta de EE.UU. sobre posible brote de peste en Siberia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Kremlin calls for calm after a U.S. alert about a possible plague outbreak in Siberia.
article.articleSummary: Possible pneumonic plague outbreak in the Irkutsk region, Siberia, after a U.S. alert; the Kremlin urges calm and to rely on Rospotrebnadzor statements. Rospotrebnadzor describes the case as pneumonia of undetermined etiology; a 28-year-old woman, an employee at the Irkutsk and Far East Plague Research Institute, died in Shélejov. Investigations consider Thailand exposure or an accidental laboratory incident as possible infection sources. None of the patient’s contacts have fallen ill or tested positive. Authorities quarantined several hospitals in Irkutsk, including a pediatric hospital, with strict restrictions on hospitalization areas and no family visits. Governor Igor Kobzev held an emergency meeting and announced contingency plans; all contacts remain under medical observation, currently asymptomatic and with negative tests. U.S. officials told Axios they continue monitoring and weighing options.

triage.headline_ja: クレムリン、米国によるシベリアでのペスト流行の可能性に関する警戒発表後、冷静な対応を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: 肺ペストの疑いで研究所職員が死亡し、米国が警戒を発するなど国際的関心が高く、IHR基準（深刻性・異常性）に複数該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: イベント発生地はロシア（イルクーツク州）であり、対象国リストに含まれない。タイは感染源候補として言及されているが、実際の発生地ではないためverified_locationsには含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Чума в Росії? Одна людина померла. Що відомо
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Plague in Russia? One person has died. What is known.
article.articleSummary: Possible pneumonic plague in Russia with one death. A 28-year-old laboratory worker at the Irkutsk Scientific Research Anti-Plague Institute in Shelekhov, Irkutsk region died after pneumonia of unknown origin. The hospital was quarantined and several departments halted admissions; the laboratory stopped analyses and other regional hospitals reportedly closed temporarily. Rosptotrebnadzor said samples from the patient did not reveal microorganisms linked to her professional work. Nearly 200 people who had contact with her are under medical surveillance; no infections have been recorded among staff in the past 10 days. Nearby officials say the death is likely from plague, but there are no confirmed outbreaks in Buryatia. The U.S. State Department is monitoring and urging transparency. WHO notes 2019–2025: over 3,800 suspected plague cases in 10 countries, mostly in DRC and Madagascar; Russia has no confirmed cases in that period per WHO. The institute, founded in 1934, historically studies plague and other dangerous infections.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアでペスト？1人死亡。分かっていること
triage.triage_reason: ロシア・イルクーツク州の抗ペスト研究所職員が原因不明の肺炎で死亡し肺ペストの疑いがあるため、異常性・重篤性が認められIHR基準に複数該当する。
triage.notes: 事例はロシア(イルクーツク州シェレホフ)の抗ペスト研究所職員の死亡であり、対象国リストに該当する国はない。記事中のDRC・マダガスカルはWHO統計（2019-2025年の世界的ペスト症例の多くがこれらの国で発生）の文脈での言及であり、本事例の発生地ではないため verified_locations には含めない。原因は確定しておらず、Rospotrebnadzorは職業関連の病原体は検出されなかったとしている。約200人の接触者を監視中だが二次感染は確認されていない。

diseases.name: Human Infection with Swine Influenza A H1N1

article.articleHeadline: H1N1 Found In 75% Of Positive Flu Tests, Dengue Hits 15,000+ Cases: What India Needs To Watch
article.articleSummary: H1N1 dominates India’s influenza activity, while dengue persists in southern states. From January–June 2026, dengue cases reached 23,952 with 31 deaths, led by Tamil Nadu (7,511 cases, 3 deaths) and Kerala (4,458 cases, 19 deaths). Five southern states together accounted for 63.2% of national dengue. Chennai recorded over 4,500 dengue cases this year; authorities expanded fever testing and intensified vector control, with DENV-2 predominating and multiple serotypes co-circulating in the region. Influenza surveillance (WHO, 1–14 Sept 2026) found A(H1N1)pdm09 in 75% of influenza-positive samples, well above the SE Asia regional average of 50%. Kerala reported 11,319 influenza cases and 120 deaths by early October 2026, with deaths rising sharply versus 2025. Older adults, pregnant women, and those with chronic conditions remain high-risk. Vaccination, respiratory hygiene, and prompt testing/treatment are urged; dengue prevention centers on eliminating mosquito breeding sites.

triage.headline_ja: H1N1がインフルエンザ陽性検査の75%を占める、デング熱は15,000件超：インドが注視すべきこと
triage.triage_reason: ケララ州でのインフルエンザ(H1N1優勢)による死亡者数が前年比で急増し、デング熱も南部諸州で高水準が続いており、公衆衛生への深刻な影響と季節外れの重症度上昇が見られるためフルリスク評価が妥当。
triage.notes: インフルエンザ(H1N1pdm09)とデング熱の季節的流行が重なっており、ケララ州での死者数急増（2025年比）が特に懸念材料。国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは現時点で示唆されていないが、続報での重症度推移の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: الأمم المتحدة تحذر من استمرار تفشي الأيبولا في شرق الكونغو - اليوم السابع
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The United Nations Warns of the Ongoing Ebola Outbreak in Eastern Congo - The Seventh Day
article.articleSummary: The United Nations reports the Ebola virus disease outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo remains active, with transmission continuing across multiple provinces. As of publication on 2026-10-05, 8,067 laboratory-confirmed cases and 3,901 deaths have been recorded, affecting 63 health zones in seven provinces. The outbreak is concentrated in Ituri and North Kivu, where active transmission persists, compounded by ongoing insecurity, population movements, displacement, and limited access to health services that hinder response and elevate transmission risk. Recent developments in North Kivu and South Kivu have driven new displacement and returns to areas with fragile services and security, further complicating containment. The UN warns of a continued significant public health risk in the region, underscoring the need for sustained containment efforts to reduce mortality and limit spread.

triage.headline_ja: 国連、コンゴ東部でのエボラ出血熱の流行継続を警告
triage.triage_reason: DRC東部で8,067例・死亡3,901例に達する大規模なエボラ流行が継続しており、治安悪化や住民移動により国際的拡大リスクも高いため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 国連報告に基づく大規模かつ継続的なエボラ流行。治安・人口移動が対応を複雑化させている。

article.articleHeadline: Dentro del estudio de un remedio para combatir el brote de ébola más mortífero del Congo | CNN
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Inside the Study of a Treatment to Combat Congo's Deadliest Ebola Outbreak | CNN
article.articleSummary: In the Democratic Republic of Congo, the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in eastern Ituri province has become the deadliest on record, with over 8,300 confirmed cases and 4,000 deaths across seven provinces, declared mid-May and continuing to outpace contact tracing. A phase of post-exposure prophylaxis trial investigates obeldesivir, an experimental antiviral pill from Gilead, given to asymptomatic contacts within five days of confirmed exposure. The ALIMA-led study aims to enroll about 1,000 participants aged 12+, randomized 1:1 to receive the pill or placebo, with daily monitoring for 21 days and a final check at 42 days. If symptoms develop, supportive care is provided. The approach aims to interrupt transmission before illness. Vaccination with Ervebo is being used for frontline workers, though effectiveness against Bundibugyo is under study.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ最悪のエボラ流行に対抗する治療薬の研究について | CNN
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最悪規模のエボラ流行（8,300例以上、死者4,000人超、7州に拡大）が継続しており、公衆衛生上の深刻な影響と異常性が明確であるためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 史上最悪規模のエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）流行で、接触者追跡が追いつかない状況。実験的抗ウイルス薬の曝露後予防投与試験（ALIMA主導）やErvebo接種が進行中。国際的な支援ニーズが高い。

article.articleHeadline: Uttar Pradesh to Run Communicable Disease Control and Dastak Campaigns in October
article.articleSummary: Uttar Pradesh will conduct a Special Communicable Disease Control Campaign from October 1–31, 2026, followed by the Dastak Campaign from October 12–31. The initiatives center on public awareness, cleanliness, symptom identification, and timely treatment. Health workers, ASHA workers, Anganwadi workers and staff from other departments will visit households across the state to engage residents, disseminate information on cleanliness, recognizing symptoms, and seeking prompt care. The household-level outreach aims to strengthen awareness of communicable diseases and promote preventive and medical actions. The Dastak Campaign overlaps with the broader Special Campaign from October 12 onward. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath cited the elimination of encephalitis in eastern Uttar Pradesh as evidence that coordinated efforts and public participation can achieve major public-health gains. The campaigns emphasize prevention, early identification, and timely treatment, combining administrative measures with community involvement to protect public health in October.

article.articleHeadline: 5 Tempat Tersembunyi di Rumah yang Bisa Jadi Sarang Nyamuk DBD, Segera Cek
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 5 Hidden Places in the Home That Could Be Breeding Grounds for Dengue-Carrying Mosquitoes, Check Now.
article.articleSummary: Hidden indoor spots can breed dengue-carrying mosquitoes, even in seemingly clean homes. A VNExpress report (5 Oct 2026) notes small amounts of standing water can accumulate unnoticed, sustaining the dengue vector. Five locations to inspect: 1) drip trays under appliances such as refrigerators, portable air conditioners, dehumidifiers, and water dispensers; empty and clean removable trays at least weekly and check for leaks. 2) Flower vases, plant containers, and saucers; replace vase water regularly, clean the containers, and pour away water from saucers after watering; eggs can cling to old water lines, so avoid overwatering. 3) Buckets, containers, and rarely used items; even bottle caps, cups, or loose bags can hold rainwater; store unused items in sheltered or inverted positions and discard what’s unnecessary. 4) Gutters, balconies, and roofs; debris can clog channels, causing pooling; inspect after rain, clean drains, secure covers, and address pools with professionals if needed.

triage.headline_ja: デング熱媒介蚊の温床になりうる家庭内の5つの隠れた場所、今すぐチェックを
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はデング熱予防に関する一般的な啓発・生活情報であり、具体的な感染拡大や症例報告を伴うものではない。
triage.notes: 記事はインドネシアのKompasが配信しているが、内容はベトナムのVNExpress記事を引用した一般的な蚊対策の生活情報であり、特定国での感染拡大事例を報じるものではないため、対象国としての特定イベントは認められない。

article.articleHeadline: Pakar UGM ingatkan bahaya penyakit antraks jika tidak segera ditangani
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: UGM experts warn of the dangers of anthrax if not treated promptly.
article.articleSummary: Anthrax (Bacillus anthracis) in Semanu, Gunungkidul, Daerah Istimewa Yogyakarta (DIY), Indonesia, is highlighted by Universitas Gadjah Mada experts as a dangerous zoonosis that can be fatal if untreated. The re-emergence of anthrax in Semanu signals ongoing animal–human transmission risk, with spores capable of persisting in the environment. Livestock deaths with high fever and loss of appetite should raise suspicion; do not slaughter or consume meat from sick or suddenly dead animals, and proper disposal of carcasses is essential. Human infection can occur via ingestion, inhalation, or skin contact with spores. Outbreaks in animals affect public health, underscoring the need for farmer and community vigilance to break transmission chains and report suspected cases to authorities. Carcasses must be destroyed. In Gunungkidul, three residents who tested positive for anthrax have recovered.

triage.headline_ja: UGMの専門家、炭疽病の危険性について速やかな対応がなければ警鐘
triage.triage_reason: インドネシア・グヌンキドゥルで炭疽の再発が確認され人獣共通感染のリスクが指摘されているが、感染者は既に回復しており大規模拡大の兆候は不明。

article.articleHeadline: الاتحاد الدولي للصليب والهلال الأحمر يندد باستهداف العاملين في مكافحة الإيبولا بالكونغو - اليوم السابع
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies condemns the targeting of workers fighting Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo - Youm7
article.articleSummary: IFRC condemns attack on Ebola response workers in the Democratic Republic of the Congo after an ambulance carrying Ebola response staff was targeted in the Aru area of Ituri Province. Ismail Molindwa, an ambulance driver with the Uganda Red Cross Society, sustained critical injuries on 17 August 2026 and died on 5 October 2026. The incident underscores the risks faced by humanitarian workers delivering Ebola outbreak response services in challenging environments. The IFRC offered condolences to Molindwa’s family, colleagues, and the Ugandan Red Cross Society, and called for protection and respect for Red Cross and Red Crescent staff and volunteers. The statement reiterates that attacks against humanitarian workers are unacceptable and highlights the ongoing Ebola response efforts in eastern DRC.

triage.headline_ja: 国際赤十字赤新月社連盟（IFRC）、コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ対応従事者への襲撃を非難
triage.triage_reason: DRC東部でのエボラ対応従事者への襲撃により救援活動が妨げられており、公衆衛生上の深刻な影響とIHR複数基準に該当するためフルRRAへ移行すべき。
triage.notes: 記事はエボラ対応従事者への襲撃事件を中心に報じており、DRC（イトゥリ州）での進行中のエボラ対応活動とその安全確保の必要性を示唆している。ウガンダ赤十字の職員が死亡したが、事件発生地はDRCであるため、verified_locationsはDRCのみとした。

article.articleHeadline: Russian Plague scare: Did a broken test tube lead to a researcher's death? Why is the White House watching and are Americans at risk?
article.articleSummary: Near Irkutsk, Russia, an incident at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute prompted fears of a plague exposure. A 28-year-old laboratory assistant, Daria Shipilova, died after severe pneumonia; authorities say the illness is pneumonia of unknown etiology, with no confirmed plague. Independent regional reports alleged she broke a vial containing a plague pathogen days before illness, but no Russian authority has verified this account. Nearly 200 contacts were monitored; initial results among contacts were negative, and authorities reported no infectious illnesses among institute staff in the previous 10 days. Rospotrebnadzor expanded tests found no microorganisms linked to Shipilova’s lab work and described the sanitary situation as stable; no confirmed emergency involving dangerous pathogens. WHO reports no confirmed international outbreak; US monitoring via White House; CDC has not issued travel warnings. Plague remains present in Madagascar and DRC, while in the US, seven human cases per year occur, typically from wildlife.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアのペスト騒動：壊れた試験管が研究者の死を招いたのか？ホワイトハウスはなぜ注視しているのか、米国民にリスクはあるのか？
triage.triage_reason: 事案はロシア・イルクーツクで発生しており対象国に該当せず、当局はペスト感染を確認しておらず接触者検査も陰性、衛生状況は安定と報告されているため見送りと判断。
triage.notes: 記事内でDRCおよびマダガスカルはペストが常在する地域として背景説明にのみ言及されており、本イベント（ロシア人研究者の死亡・検疫対応）の発生地ではないためverified_locationsには含めない。対象国（ザンビア、フィリピン等）とは無関係な事案。

article.articleHeadline: Dentro del estudio de un remedio para combatir el brote de ébola más mortífero del Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Inside the Study of a Remedy to Combat the Congo's Most Deadly Ebola Outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Eastern Congo's Bundibugyo strain Ebola outbreak has produced at least 8,300 confirmed cases and 4,000 deaths across seven provinces since mid-May, with Ituri province as an epicenter. In an ALIMA-led trial begun in July, more than 250 participants aged 12 and older who had recent exposure are testing obeldesivir as post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) to prevent disease; about half receive a placebo, with daily monitoring for 21 days and a final check at 42 days. The goal is to interrupt transmission by protecting individuals before symptoms appear, distinct from vaccines or curative treatments. Frontline vaccination with Ervebo is underway, but its efficacy against Bundibugyo is unproven. Recruitment has been hampered by difficult contact tracing and emotional challenges in households; MSF is among collaborating partners, as researchers seek to curb the outbreak and prevent further spread.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ最悪のエボラ流行に対抗する治療薬研究の内側
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）がDRC東部で8,300症例・4,000死亡という大規模な流行を起こしており、IHR基準の複数（深刻性・異常性・国際拡大リスク）に該当するためフルRRAへの移行が妥当。
triage.notes: 既に進行中の大規模エボラ流行（ブンディブギョ株）に関する治療薬治験の記事。既知アウトブレイクの継続報道だが、規模（8,300症例・4,000死亡）と国際的対応（ALIMA、MSF参加）から引き続き注視・評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: В результате эпидемии Эболы в Конго умерли 4 114 человек
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: As a result of the Ebola epidemic in Congo, 4,114 people died.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-10-05, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reached 8,854 cases and 4,114 deaths (case fatality 48.2%). About 824 symptomatic patients remain in hospitals or medical isolation. Infections have been reported in the 64th health zone; the country has 519 health zones, with fever outbreaks affecting 7 of 26 provinces. The epidemic began in May in Congo and neighboring Uganda, now the second-deadliest Ebola outbreak on Africa’s history. In Bunia, Ituri Province, the first volunteers were vaccinated with the Ervebo Ebola vaccine, and in August about 70,000 doses of Ervebo were allocated for vaccination efforts.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行で4,114人が死亡
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で患者8,854人・死者4,114人（致死率48.2%）に達し、アフリカ史上2番目に深刻なエボラ流行となっており、複数州・隣国への拡大も確認されているため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ウガンダへの感染拡大が報じられているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。致死率48.2%は極めて高く、アフリカ史上2番目に深刻なエボラ流行との記載あり。

article.articleHeadline: Poznati splitski infektolog komentira šokantnu pojavu kuge: 'Teško je povjerovati u priču o razbijenoj epruveti...'
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A renowned Split-based infectious disease specialist comments on the shocking appearance of the plague: "It's hard to believe the story about the broken test tube..."
article.articleSummary: In Selekhov, Siberia, Russia, a young laboratory technician, Darija Shipilova, died of plague, triggering quarantine for nearly 200 people in the Irkutsk region amid accusations of a cover-up. Ana Popova, head of Russia’s public health service, traveled to Irkutsk as the hospital was placed under quarantine and dozens of contacts were placed under strict medical surveillance. Renowned epidemiologist Mikhal Favorov questions the broken-test-tube explanation, suggesting the situation may be more serious and noting that workers at the plague institute wear protective gear; a shattered vial would not easily cause an outbreak. Croatian infectious-disease expert Ivo Ivić says contracting plague from a broken vial is unlikely and stresses precautionary isolation due to possible exposure. The piece notes Europe has not seen plague for decades, while it persists in India (mostly bubonic) and the southern United States; bubonic plague is rodent-flea–transmitted, and pneumonic plague rapidly damages the lungs.

triage.headline_ja: 著名なスプリトの感染症専門家が衝撃的なペスト発生について言及：「割れた試験管の話は信じがたい」
triage.triage_reason: ロシア・イルクーツク州でペストにより研究技術者が死亡し、約200人が隔離される事態が発生。欧州では数十年ぶりの事例であり、研究所での事故説に専門家が疑義を呈するなど異常性と社会的関心が高い。
triage.notes: イベントの発生地はロシア・イルクーツク州であり、対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsは空。記事中でインドや米国が言及されているが、これは単なる疫学的背景情報（ペストが風土病として存在する地域）であり、本イベントの発生地ではないため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: 10歲男童染甲流併發休克留醫　開學後350校爆發涉逾2000人
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A 10-year-old boy infected with influenza A (H1N1) developed shock and was hospitalized; after school resumed, outbreaks in 350 schools affected more than 2,000 people.
article.articleSummary: As of 5 October 2026, in Hong Kong, a 10-year-old boy infected with influenza A (H1N1) developed shock and was admitted to the Prince of Wales Hospital PICU. He presented last Friday with fever, cough, runny nose, and dizziness; laboratory testing confirmed influenza A (H1N1) with shock. He had no recent travel and had not received the 2026/27 seasonal influenza vaccine. A household contact recently showed mild symptoms and recovered. Since late June, Hong Kong’s flu season has remained highly active, with about 350 school-based influenza-like illness outbreaks after school resumed, affecting more than 2,000 people. In total, 22 pediatric influenza severe cases have been reported this season: 16 recovered/discharged, 2 stable, 2 serious, 1 critical, and 1 death. Public health authorities will continue monitoring the situation.

triage.headline_ja: 10歳の男児がA型インフルエンザ（H1N1）に感染しショック状態で入院　新学期開始後、350校で2000人超が発症

article.articleHeadline: Plicní mor: jaké jsou příznaky, jak se šíří a proč je nejnebezpečnější formou nemoci
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Pneumonic Plague: What Are the Symptoms, How It Spreads, and Why It Is the Most Dangerous Form of the Disease.
article.articleSummary: Pneumonic plague, caused by Yersinia pestis, is the most dangerous form and can be rapidly fatal without prompt antibiotics. Transmission occurs by inhalation of infectious droplets from a patient, enabling person-to-person spread; it can also arise from animals. Early antibiotic treatment is critical; WHO notes death can occur within 18–24 hours if untreated, while timely care improves outcomes. Diagnosis relies on lab testing of blood or sputum, but treatment should begin on plausible clinical suspicion. Endemic in Madagascar and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Madagascar reported 51 cases in 2025; major outbreaks occurred in 2017 around Antananarivo and Toamasina, with activity in 2021 in Itasy and Haute Matsiatra. Notable imported/exported cases include 2019 detections in Inner Mongolia/Beijing, 2021 Wyoming, and a July 2025 death in Coconino County, Arizona linked to exposure to ill cats. Russia denied an outbreak but reported quarantines in Irkutsk Oblast; U.S. and health authorities monitor.

triage.headline_ja: 肺ペスト：症状は何か、どのように広がるか、なぜ最も危険な病型なのか
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は肺ペストに関する一般的・教育的な解説記事であり、過去の既知事例（マダガスカル2025年、2017年・2021年の流行、2019年中国、2021年米国）をまとめたものであって、新規の発生や進行中のアウトブレイクを報じるものではない。
triage.notes: 記事は疾患解説が中心で、マダガスカル・中国・DRC等への言及はあるが、いずれも過去の既知事例の紹介にとどまり、現時点での新規発生や進行中のアウトブレイクを示す情報はない。マダガスカルは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。中国・DRCについても具体的な現在進行中の症例情報がなく、現状報告としての根拠が弱いためverified_locationsは空とした。

article.articleHeadline: Russia plague scare: India's past outbreak and concerns around latest episode
article.articleSummary: A 28-year-old laboratory worker in Irkutsk, Russia, died after severe pneumonia, with about 200 people under medical observation for possible exposure; authorities have not confirmed plague, labeling the illness pneumonia of unknown origin, though Russian media report possible Yersinia pestis exposure at an anti-plague institute. The epidemiological situation in the region remains described as stable, but international attention and expert concern persist. US health authorities and Dr. Ashish Jha have called for vigilance rather than confirmation of an outbreak. The incident echoes India's 1994 plague experience, which included 63 bubonic cases in Mamla (Beed district, Maharashtra) and a larger Surat outbreak with 876 cases and 54 deaths, underscoring plague’s zoonotic nature and the importance of rodent and flea surveillance. Plague arises from Yersinia pestis; three forms exist—bubonic, pneumonic, septicaemic—with pneumonic plague posing the greatest human-to-human transmission risk and requiring early antibiotic treatment.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアでのペスト警戒:インドの過去の流行と最新事例への懸念
triage.triage_reason: ロシア・イルクーツクの研究所職員が原因不明の重症肺炎で死亡し、約200人が曝露観察下に置かれ、Yersinia pestis関連の可能性が報じられている。重症例・異常性・国際的注目度の高さからフルリスク評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Pneumonic plague: What to know about the disease after suspected case in Siberia
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-10-05, about 200 people in Irkutsk, eastern Siberia, are under medical observation after an Anti-Plague Institute employee died of suspected plague on Oct 2. Darya Shipilova reportedly broke a test tube containing Yersinia pestis and developed suspected pneumonic plague after returning from a work trip to Buryatia near the Mongolia border, where an outbreak had been reported. Expanded testing found no microorganisms linked to her lab work. The Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute monitors high-risk infections across Siberia and the Far East. Pneumonic plague is the most virulent form, with a short incubation and transmission via inhaled droplets; it is treatable with antibiotics, especially if treated within 24 hours, but untreated pneumonic plague is typically fatal. Globally, plague is relatively uncommon, with current hotspots in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Madagascar; 2019–2025 WHO data show 3,860 suspected cases, 2,646 confirmed, 423 deaths.

triage.headline_ja: 肺ペスト：シベリアでの疑い例発生後に知っておくべきこと
triage.triage_reason: ロシア・シベリアで研究所職員が肺ペストの疑いで死亡し、約200人が経過観察下にあるなど、重篤性と異常性が高くIHR基準を2つ以上満たすため、フルリスク評価に進むべき事案と判断した。

article.articleHeadline: Pestiskarantén Szibériában
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Plague quarantine in Siberia
article.articleSummary: Published 2026-10-05. In Siberia, a plague quarantine is under way after 28-year-old Darja Sipilova, a laboratory technician at Irkutsk’s Pest Institute, died two days after admission on Sept 29 with fever and severe respiratory distress. Competing theories link infection to a Thailand trip or to a laboratory accident with a broken vial. Officially, Sipilova died of pneumonia of unknown etiology; no pathogen tied to her work was found. Nevertheless, doctors openly discuss pneumonic plague, triggering containment: three-week selective quarantines at Irkutsk hospitals 1, 3, and 10, Ivano‑Matreninskaya Children’s Hospital, and a maternity hospital. At least 197 people have been isolated; Anna Popova, Russia’s chief physician, flew to the site for closed-door talks. Authorities report information controls and removal of plague-related reports. Pneumonic plague spreads by droplets, with 24–48 hour incubation and near-100% untreated mortality; plague persists in natural foci in Siberia, Central Asia, and parts of North America.

triage.headline_ja: シベリアでペスト検疫
triage.triage_reason: 肺ペストの疑いによる大規模隔離と情報統制が報告されており重大性は高いが、病原体の確定や対象国（タイ等）での感染拡大は未確認のため続報を注視する。

article.articleHeadline: Persiapan Haji dan Umrah, Jemaah Diminta Waspadai Risiko Pneumonia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Preparation for Hajj and Umrah, Pilgrims Urged to Be Wary of Pneumonia Risk
article.articleSummary: Pneumonia risk for Hajj and Umrah pilgrims, especially older adults and those with diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, or stroke, is emphasized in Pfizer Indonesia’s 'Lindungi Napasmu, Jaga Momen Berarti' campaign. A YouGov survey of Muslim respondents shows 43% plan to perform Hajj/Umrah within two years, with crowded conditions increasing exposure to respiratory infections. Only 11% recognise crowds as a source of risk for serious pneumonia. Pneumococcal pneumonia, caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, differs from influenza, though both affect the respiratory tract; upper respiratory infections can progress to pneumonia. Risks during the pilgrimage include fatigue from long flights, jet lag, climate changes, dehydration, and comorbidity. Recommendations: adequate rest, hydration, handwashing, and masking in crowded places, plus medical check-ups about six months before departure following government guidelines. Clinicians highlight controlling chronic conditions to reduce pneumonia risk in Saudi Arabia’s Mecca and Medina and on return to Indonesia.

triage.headline_ja: ハジ・ウムラ準備、巡礼者は肺炎リスクに注意するよう呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: 特定の感染症アウトブレイクの報告ではなく、製薬会社による肺炎予防啓発キャンペーンの一般的な健康情報記事であり、トリアージ基準に該当しない。
triage.notes: 本記事は具体的な感染症の発生・流行を報告するものではなく、肺炎球菌性肺炎とインフルエンザに関する一般的な予防啓発（製薬会社のキャンペーン）が内容。サウジアラビア（メッカ・メディナ）やインドネシアは対象国リストに含まれないため、verified_locationsは空。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola outbreak has passed its peak - DR Congo -- RT Africa
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo has passed its peak, according to the health ministry, with transmission now concentrated in a smaller number of health zones rather than across provinces. Of 63 health zones under surveillance, 12 have recorded no new cases for at least 42 days, and eight zones 22–42 days without reporting infections. Contacts being monitored rose to about 82% by September 28, up from 28% in May. As of October 2, the country reported 66 new confirmed cases and 38 deaths, bringing totals to 8,442 infections and 4,080 deaths (case fatality rate 48.3%). Despite the apparent decline, Africa CDC warns that insecurity and disrupted surveillance, especially in eastern Congo, can mask ongoing transmission; 45 of 63 zones still report active transmission. WHO echoes concerns; instability linked to M23 clashes continues to fuel humanitarian emergencies.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱の流行はピークを過ぎた - コンゴ民主共和国
triage.triage_reason: 致死率48.3%、累計4,080人死亡という重大な公衆衛生インパクトがあり、M23紛争による治安悪化でサーベイランスが阻害され国際的拡大・管理困難のリスクが残るため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 既知の継続中のアウトブレイクだが、治安悪化による監視能力低下で感染拡大が隠蔽されるリスクがWHO・Africa CDCにより指摘されており、注視継続が必要。

article.articleHeadline: डासांचा प्रादुर्भाव वाढला : औषध व धूर फवारणीची नागरिकांची मागणी
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Mosquito infestation has increased: Citizens demand pesticides and fogging.
article.articleSummary: As of 5 October 2026, Satpur area reports a sharp rise in mosquito infestation, prompting residents to demand pesticides and fogging. Stagnant dirty drainage water and heaps of garbage on streets have increased dengue and malaria fears. Residents say mosquitoes are most problematic mornings and evenings. Hospitals—public and private—are seeing more patients with fever, body ache, and other symptoms. Citizens urge the municipal health department to promptly locate and eliminate breeding sites and to implement regular, permanent fogging and pesticide spraying. Some measures are claimed to be ongoing ward-wise, with loudspeaker notices to raise awareness. Quotes from Narayan Jadhav of the Malaria Department and Kamalabai Ingale, a local, underline the demand for intensified, sustained interventions beyond mere complaints.

triage.headline_ja: 蚊の発生が増加：住民が殺虫剤散布と燻蒸を要求
triage.triage_reason: インドのサトプール地区で蚊媒介感染症（デング熱・マラリア）への懸念が高まっているが、具体的な症例数や重症度のデータが不足しており、地域の衛生インフラ問題に起因するローカルな事案と見られる。
triage.notes: 地元住民と保健当局（マラリア部門）が対応を求めているローカルニュースであり、発熱患者の増加が報告されているが確定症例数や死亡者数などの具体的データはない。排水溝の滞留水やゴミの放置による蚊の繁殖地問題が背景にある。

article.articleHeadline: Suspected Pneumonic Plague Death In Russia Sparks Concern, Kerala IMA Expert Says No Immediate Threat To India
article.articleSummary: Russia investigates a suspected pneumonic plague death; case unverified and authorities are tracing contacts. A Kerala IMA expert said there is no immediate threat to India and urged against panic, noting cause of death is not yet confirmed. Yersinia pestis is the bacterium behind plague, which can manifest as skin, pneumonic (lung), or septicemic forms. Pneumonic plague is the most dangerous and can rapidly progress to death in about 24 hours. Key control measures include rapid contact tracing and antibiotic prophylaxis for those at close risk. India is not considered at risk via travel, as severely ill patients are typically unlikely to travel, and transmission depends on setting. CDC notes pneumonic plague symptoms as fever, headache, weakness, rapidly developing pneumonia, breathing difficulties, chest pain, cough, and sputum that may be bloody or watery. Ongoing Russia investigation involves contact tracing; no confirmed outbreak in India."

triage.headline_ja: ロシアでの肺ペスト疑い死亡例が懸念を呼ぶ、ケララIMA専門家はインドへの直接的な脅威はないと発言
triage.triage_reason: ロシアで未確認の肺ペスト疑い死亡例が報告され調査中だが、確定診断・流行拡大の証拠はなく、インドへの直接的影響も専門家により否定されている。対象国での確認事例はないため、続報を注視する段階。
triage.notes: 事例発生地はロシア（対象国リスト外）であり、インドでは症例未確認。ケララIMA専門家のコメントは国内への脅威否定のためのもので、実際の国内発生ではない。確定診断・追加症例の有無を今後注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Experte erklärt, wie gefährlich Lungenpest wirklich ist
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: An expert explains how dangerous pneumonic plague really is
article.articleSummary: 28-year-old laboratory staffer at an institute studying plague pathogens in Irkutsk, Siberia, dies; initial suspicion of pneumonic plague, later official claim attributes death to pneumonia of unknown origin. Infec­tion-epidemiologist Prof. Timo Ulrichs warns that untreated pneumonic plague is 100% fatal and that when bacteria reach the lungs, human-to-human transmission via respiratory droplets is possible. Early symptoms are fever, cough, and sputum, with potential progression to bloody sputum; incubation can be as short as about 24 hours. The case is under investigation; Russian regulator Rospotrebnadsor says there was no laboratory accident and the deceased’s samples contained no microorganisms linked to her work. Ulrichs urges transparent investigation with WHO involvement. Globally, plague persists in Madagascar and Congo, with smaller outbreaks in Russia; Germany faces extremely low risk, and contact tracing/isolation have been implemented. No cases in Germany reported by authorities; overall risk of export to Europe deemed very low.

triage.headline_ja: 専門家が肺ペストの実際の危険性を解説
triage.triage_reason: ロシア・イルクーツクのペスト研究機関職員が原因不明の肺炎で死亡し、肺ペストの疑いが報じられるという異例の事例であり、専門家がヒト-ヒト感染リスクやWHO関与の必要性を指摘するなど社会的関心が高いため、フルRRAでの精査が望ましい。
triage.notes: 事例発生地はロシア（イルクーツク）であり、対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsは空配列。記事中で言及されるDRC・マダガスカルは背景情報としてのペスト流行地であり、本事例の主題ではないため除外。ロシア当局は研究所事故を否定し、死因を原因不明の肺炎としているため、肺ペストであるか不確実性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: Varios hospitales de Siberia en cuarentena por sospechas de un brote de peste pulmonar originado por una investigadora
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Several hospitals in Siberia under quarantine due to suspicions of a pneumonic plague outbreak originating from a female researcher.
article.articleSummary: In Irkutsk region, Siberia, several hospitals were quarantined over suspicions of pneumonic plague linked to a female researcher. Rospotrebnadzor attributed the death of a 28-year-old employee of the Institute of Plague Research of Irkutsk and the Far East to pneumonia of unknown etiology and is evaluating whether the infection occurred in Thailand or resulted from an accidental laboratory incident involving a tube of pathogens. At least four medical facilities, including a pediatric hospital, have imposed quarantines of up to three weeks; hospitalization wards are restricted and visitors barred. Authorities say those who contacted the patient are under medical observation; as of now, none show symptoms and all tests are negative. No official confirmation of plague has been issued. The Kremlin urged calm and to rely on official statements from Rospotrebnadzor.

triage.headline_ja: シベリアの複数の病院が、女性研究者に起因する肺ペスト流行の疑いで隔離措置
triage.triage_reason: ペスト研究所職員の原因不明肺炎による死亡と複数病院の隔離措置という重大かつ異常な事象であり、IHR基準（深刻性・異常性）を2つ満たすためフルRRAへの移行が必要。
triage.notes: 実際の発生地はロシア・イルクーツク州であり対象国リストに含まれない。タイでの感染可能性は調査中の推測段階であり、記事の主題はロシアでの事象であるためタイは含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Imponen cuarentena en al menos cuatro centros sanitarios de Siberia por sospechas de peste pulmonar
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Quarantine imposed in at least four health centers in Siberia due to suspected pneumonic plague.
article.articleSummary: Suspected pneumonic plague in the Irkutsk region, Siberia, triggers quarantine in at least four hospitals with airborne transmission risk. Hospital areas are strictly restricted and visits barred; one center is pediatric; measures may extend up to three weeks. Authorities have not explicitly named the pathogen, though regional officials held an emergency meeting over suspicion of exposure to a highly dangerous infection, with no confirmed case reported. All contacts are under medical observation; as of now, none show symptoms and all tests are negative. A 28-year-old woman, employee at the Institute of Plague Research of Irkutsk and the Far East, died last week in Shélejov. Possible sources include infection in Thailand or a laboratory accident involving a broken tube with pathogens at her workplace. Rospotrebnadzor labeled the diagnosis as pneumonia of undetermined etiology. Pneumonic plague, caused by Yersinia pestis, is highly contagious by air but curable with antibiotics when detected early.

triage.headline_ja: シベリアの少なくとも4つの医療施設で肺ペスト疑いにより隔離措置
triage.triage_reason: 肺ペスト疑いによる病院隔離と研究所職員の死亡事例があり、重篤性・異常性の観点からIHR基準を2つ満たすためフルリスク評価に進むべきと判断。
triage.notes: 事件はロシア・イルクーツク州（シベリア）で発生しており、タイは感染源の可能性として言及されているのみで実際の発生地ではないため、対象国リストには該当しない。病原体の確定診断は未了（Rospotrebnadzorは『原因不明の肺炎』と分類）。

article.articleHeadline: मच्छर जनित रोगों से बचाव के लिए ग्रामीणों को किया जागरूक
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Villagers educated on protection against mosquito-borne diseases
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-10-05, in Badayun district, India, District Malaria Officer Amit Kumar Tiwari visited Sarva village in Block Bisouli to reinforce prevention of vector-borne diseases, notably dengue and malaria. A larvicide spray was conducted to curb mosquito breeding, and stock was provided to the village head for ongoing use. The outreach extended to schools, where children were educated on protective measures and recognition of vector-borne illnesses. Residents were advised to eliminate standing water around homes, wear full-sleeve clothing, and use mosquito nets. The campaign emphasizes routine surveillance and community participation to reduce transmission, with health teams urging vigilance against dengue, malaria, and other related diseases.

triage.headline_ja: 蚊媒介性疾患からの予防について村民に啓発
triage.triage_reason: 通常の予防啓発活動・公衆衛生教育に関する記事であり、異常な発生や重大な公衆衛生上の脅威を示す情報は含まれていない。
triage.notes: 記事はインド・ウッタル・プラデーシュ州Budaun県での定期的な予防啓発・防蚊対策活動を報じるもので、具体的な症例数や流行の急増を示す情報はない。

article.articleHeadline: France Reaffirms Support for Ebola Combat Efforts in DRC
article.articleSummary: France reaffirms support for Ebola response in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot visiting Bunia, the outbreak epicenter and site of the command center opened last May. The outbreak has registered approximately 8,000 confirmed cases and about 4,000 deaths, roughly a quarter of them children. Containment to date has prevented spread to major urban centers in Africa, French overseas territories, or Europe. France says it mobilized from day one to aid researchers, health workers, and humanitarian staff, emphasizing that viruses recognize no borders and that eradicating Ebola requires addressing the source. Barrot praised French researchers and humanitarian workers on the front lines for saving lives and limiting transmission, reaffirming Paris's ongoing commitment to funding and logistical support.

triage.headline_ja: フランス、コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ対応支援を改めて表明
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で約8000例・4000人死亡という大規模エボラ流行が継続しており、国際的な支援活動も行われていることから、フルリスク評価が必要と判断。
triage.notes: 記事はフランスによるDRCエボラ対応支援に関する内容であり、発生国はDRCのみ。フランスやパリは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。感染の国際的拡大は現時点で抑制されているが、エボラの性質上リスクは継続していると評価。

article.articleHeadline: Новые штаммы вирусов гриппа в России в 2026: что известно
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: New strains of influenza viruses in Russia in 2026: what is known.
article.articleSummary: Influenza in Russia is stable for the current season, with all three vaccine components updated, indicating circulation of new strains to which the population has little immunity. The strains were previously detected in Hong Kong last year; the World Health Organization studied them and based on antigens, developed a new vaccine. October is the optimal vaccination time, allowing immunity to develop before the season peak. This is a normal yearly mutation; unlike COVID-19, influenza is well studied, and scientists forecast active strains. Symptoms of the new strains are the same as ordinary flu and cannot be distinguished without PCR. The main danger are complications—pneumonia, myocarditis, and bronchitis—potentially serious or lifelong. Vaccination does not fully prevent infection but greatly reduces risk of severe disease and hospitalization. There is no natural immunity in Russia to these strains; vaccination remains the best protection, especially for the elderly, chronically ill, and service workers.

triage.headline_ja: 2026年ロシアにおけるインフルエンザ新株について：何が分かっているか
triage.triage_reason: 通常の季節性インフルエンザのワクチン接種を呼びかける内容であり、異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。対象国での発生でもない。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はロシアにおける季節性インフルエンザのワクチン接種推奨であり、ロシアは対象国リストに含まれない。香港での株検出は昨年の既往歴として言及されているのみで、現在のイベントの発生地ではないため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: ஆய்வகத்திலிருந்து வெளியேறிய ஆபத்தான வைரஸ்.. இந்தியர்களுக்கு பாதிப்பா? நிபுணர்கள் சொல்லும் பதில்!
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A dangerous virus that escaped from the laboratory... Will it affect Indians? What experts say.
article.articleSummary: Pneumonic plague linked to a laboratory accident in Russia’s Siberia, Irkutsk region, at an Anti-Black Research Institute. A 28-year-old researcher, Dariya Shibilova, unintentionally broke a tube containing a highly dangerous germ, leading to a leak.
